title: Workers have no home: a multi-site group cannot record which site a worker belongs to
persona: HR manager at Northern Care Group (400 staff, 8 sites)
evidence:
Verified against the code and the live API as admin@northern-care-group.example (org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n, 9 sites, 414 workers):

- Schema: apps/api/src/db/schema.ts workers table (lines 126-154) has orgId but no site or home column. sites (line 95), capacityFlags.siteId (line 199) and shifts.siteId (line 217) carry a site.
- Worker validation: apps/api/src/routes/workers.ts zWorker (lines 16-35) has no siteId, and zod strips unknown keys.
- POST /api/v1/workers {firstName, lastName, jobRole, siteId:<Bolton site_jgdz2lot1dsta4tn>} returned 201. The response has no siteId or homeSiteId, so the field was dropped silently. This confirms the finding's claim for the siteId half. I did not re-test the finding's documents:[...] half (also dropped, per the finding).
- PATCH /workers/wrk_dhks6qtspa31pssb {siteId, homeSiteId} returned 200 with the worker unchanged and no home field.
- GET /workers?siteId=<real Bolton site> returned 414 rows, the same as the unfiltered list. The route's query schema (workers.ts line 56) only accepts orgId, status and jobRole, and unknown params are ignored. The finding's 413 is the pre-existing 400 plus the 13 starters created earlier; 414 now includes the persona's data.
- The worker response keys (compliance, contractedHoursPerWeek, createdAt, email, firstName, hourlyPayRate, id, jobRole, lastName, lat, lng, maxHoursPerWeek, notes, optedOutOf48h, orgId, phone, postcode, shareable, skills, status, travelRadiusKm, updatedAt, userId) contain nothing site-like.
- POST /organisations/org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n/users {role:ORG_MANAGER, siteId} returned 201 with no site on the user. The route's zod schema (routes/organisations.ts lines 224-232) has no siteId and the users table has no site column. This is the ONB-03 side.
- GET /timesheets?scope=receivable returned 63 rows. Each carries worker {id, firstName, lastName, jobRole} and shift, but nothing about the worker's home.
- GET /organisations/:id/stats returned shiftsSupplied 8 and hoursSupplied 72.5. The code (organisations.ts lines 60-82) sums scheduled shift hours of CONFIRMED and COMPLETED assignments by assignment createdAt, over a rolling 30 days, with no site dimension. It is therefore on a different basis from timesheet hours. I could not reproduce the finding's 55.0h and 76.7h: by approvedAt I got 95.3h for the 30 days and 84.0h for April on 59 approved receivable timesheets. The basis mismatch is real, but the exact comparison figures are not reliable.
- The capacity flag does accept siteId, and the Capacity page has an optional site selector (CapacityPage.tsx lines 132-135). But services/capacity.ts only stores it and does nothing with it. With no worker-to-site link, "pause lending from two homes" cannot be enforced at worker level.
- Web: WorkersPage and WorkerDetailPage reference no site. The API reference (docs/API.md) lists no worker site.

Cleanup after my probes: I created a probe worker (wrk_vtzgf4601dkt6e8q, set INACTIVE; DELETE is not supported and returned 404) and a probe manager (usr_lpvjv8me80kbaxiz, set DISABLED) in Northern Care Group.
impact: Every question a 400-staff, 8-home group asks is unanswerable on the platform: who is at which home, pause one home, report one home, give one home's manager a scoped view. HR keeps the home mapping in a spreadsheet and the platform's data (and any future ONB-03 / REP-02 work) has nothing to join to.
proposal:
Smallest sensible change:
1. Add a nullable homeSiteId on workers (FK to sites; same-org check as capacity.ts does at line 70).
2. Accept it on POST and PATCH /workers (and on any future importer), and return it on the worker.
3. Add a siteId filter to GET /workers.
4. Show a Home column, filter and edit field on the Workers page and worker detail.
5. Stamp the supplier's homeSiteId onto the assignment and timesheet rows at creation. Then ONB-03's site-scoped manager role and REP-02's by-home hours report both have something to join to.
6. Optionally let a SURPLUS capacity flag's existing siteId select only workers whose home matches, which would deliver the "pause lending from a home" task.

Ship the schema and API change first (small), then the UI column and filter. Leave the scoped manager role (ONB-03) and the reports (REP-02) as separate follow-ups on top.
decisionNeeded: 1) Does a worker belong to exactly one home, or can float/bank staff attach to several? A single nullable homeSiteId is the smallest option; a join table is the flexible one. 2) Should a home move be dated (effective-from history) so past reports stay attributed to the old home, or is a plain overwrite acceptable at first? 3) Should the home be visible to host organisations (currently workers are shown to hosts without private fields), or private to the employer like hourlyPayRate?

title: Deactivating a worker leaves their login live: a leaver can still see bookings and submit timesheets
persona: HR manager at Northern Care Group (400 staff, 8 sites)
evidence: Live repro on 2027-05-03 frozen clock. (1) POST /shifts/shf_na5xwa4jbcv772o7/requests {workerId: wrk_fw2k7sit9450ye3y} -> 201 CONFIRMED (asg_syussl2i5nwogaqp). (2) PATCH /workers/wrk_fw2k7sit9450ye3y {status:INACTIVE} -> 200, nothing else changed. (3) As the leaver (eli.adeyemi.378@northern-care-group.example / Temp-Pass-1234): POST /auth/login -> 200; GET /auth/me -> 200 (worker.status INACTIVE, user.status ACTIVE); GET /assignments?scope=outgoing -> 200 with the CONFIRMED booking; GET /shifts/shf_na5xwa4jbcv772o7 -> 200 including site address and accessNotes with the staff door keypad code; POST /timesheets/ts_16hj5r30h00aoa2n/submit {clockInAt 07:00, clockOutAt 14:30 on 2027-05-10, breakMinutes 30} -> 200 SUBMITTED, paidHours 7, hostCost 126, supplierAmount 115.92, and visible as SUBMITTED to Meadow View. (4) GET /workers?status=INACTIVE -> 200, 6 rows, no upcoming or bookings field (keys: id, orgId, userId, ..., compliance); upcoming exists only on GET /workers/:id. (5) Role split: as rota@northern-care-group.example (ORG_MANAGER), PATCH /workers/:id -> 200 but PATCH /organisations/:id/users/:userId -> 403, because organisations.ts:253 uses requireRole(...ADMINS). A rota manager can mark someone inactive and cancel their bookings but cannot kill the login; only an org admin can. (6) Persona's step count holds: per leaver 1 PATCH worker + 1 GET worker + n cancels + 1 PATCH user, so 3 leavers with one booking each is 12 calls plus 1 list call = 13. Code: apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:81, apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts:44, apps/api/src/routes/workers.ts (PATCH /:id), apps/api/src/services/timesheets.ts (assertBookingLive; submitTimes and approve have no started-check), apps/api/src/routes/organisations.ts:253-263. Not in docs/API.md: no offboard endpoint.
impact: A leaver keeps access to where and when the group's staff are working and can create a payable timesheet; HR has to remember three separate screens per leaver, and the step most likely to be forgotten (disable the user) is the security-relevant one.
proposal: Smallest sensible change, in three parts. (a) Make requireAuth and login reject a WORKER-role user whose linked worker is not ACTIVE (one extra lookup keyed on user.workerId), so INACTIVE immediately kills the session with 401 'Account is not active' and no second step can be forgotten. This is about 6 lines and is the security-critical fix. (b) Add POST /workers/:id/offboard, or make PATCH /workers/:id with status INACTIVE do it, usable by ORG_MANAGER as well as admins: it withdraws REQUESTED/OFFERED, cancels CONFIRMED future assignments with a non-penalised reason (cancellation by the supplier within the late window still counts as lateCancellation today, so pass a flag or reason code that suppresses it), closes draft timesheets via the existing closeTimesheetForEndedBooking, optionally sets the linked user DISABLED, and returns {cancelled:[...], withdrawn:[...], timesheetsClosed:n, loginDisabled}. (c) Add upcomingCount (or hasUpcoming) to GET /workers rows and a 'still booked' badge on the inactive-workers list in WorkersPage. Related hardening, not required here: reject timesheet submit/clock-out before the shift has started or with times outside the shift window (this also protects against active workers submitting early), and stop returning accessNotes (door codes) until close to the shift start.
decisionNeeded: Whether a leaver's confirmed future bookings are auto-cancelled (host notified, shift reopened to the network, with the cancellation exempt from late-cancellation penalties) or flagged for the rota manager to re-cover first. Also whether an ORG_MANAGER (rota manager) may disable a worker's login or only an org admin, and whether setting a worker INACTIVE should always disable the login (with re-enabling on reactivation) or whether some employers want leavers to keep read-only access to payslips and history.

title: A home manager login is a whole-group manager: sees and can change every worker's private pay, edits and deletes any site
persona: HR manager at Northern Care Group (400 staff, 8 sites)
evidence:
Verified live against http://localhost:4055 (clock 2027-05-03) and in code.

1. Site scope is dropped on user create. As Northern admin, POST /api/v1/organisations/org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n/users with {role:ORG_MANAGER, siteId:"x", siteIds:["x"]} returned 201 and the user object had no site field. The zod schema at apps/api/src/routes/organisations.ts:227-237 has no site field and silently strips unknown keys. There is no site column on users in db/schema.ts; siteId appears only at schema.ts:199 (capacity_flags) and :217 (shifts). PATCH /users/:userId (line 260) can only change role, status and name.

2. A plain ORG_MANAGER has group-wide worker data. As the new verify.bolton.manager@ ORG_MANAGER (rota@ behaves the same), GET /workers returned 200 with 415 rows; 412 of them carried a non-null hourlyPayRate. workers.ts:45-49 stripPrivate only strips pay and notes when the viewer is outside the worker's org. The notes field is present on every row, though all were null in this sample.

3. Writes work. PATCH /workers/wrk_a9jikk2a4vqsc1oc {hourlyPayRate:99} returned 200 and a re-read showed 99. I restored the original 12.3 (200). The route is requireRole(...MANAGERS) with no field-level restriction (workers.ts:~128).

4. Sites are fully editable. POST /sites returned 201, PATCH /sites/:id {accessNotes} returned 200, and DELETE /sites/:id returned 204 for a throwaway site I created. All three are requireRole(...MANAGERS) with only assertOrgAccess (organisations.ts:113-158). DELETE is blocked with 409 if the site has any shift (lines 149-152). The Didsbury PATCH was not run on real data, but it has the same code path.

5. Stats are group-wide. GET /organisations/:id/stats returned 200 with the whole group's posted shifts, spend and earnings (organisations.ts:55-85, MANAGERS, no site filter).

6. Restricted for managers. GET /organisations/:id/users returned 403. Users, org PATCH, relationships and invoices are all ADMINS-only.

Test residue: the created user usr_xv2n1wlpe7uqd5of (verify.bolton.manager@northern-care-group.example) is left DISABLED, because there is no user delete. The worker's pay was restored, and the throwaway site was deleted. Pre-existing bolton.manager@northern-care-group.example is an ORG_MANAGER with the same powers.
impact: The group cannot delegate rota management to home managers without exposing pay for all 400 staff and allowing a home manager to alter pay or remove another home's site; this is a data-protection and HR-confidentiality blocker for a group, on top of the scoping gap in ONB-03.
proposal: Smallest sensible change, in two steps. (a) Permission split, no new data model needed. Make ORG_MANAGER read-only on hourlyPayRate and notes by extending stripPrivate to strip them unless the viewer is ORG_ADMIN or PLATFORM_ADMIN. Reject hourlyPayRate and notes in PATCH and POST /workers for ORG_MANAGER. Move site DELETE and site PATCH/POST to ADMINS, and leave managers able to read sites. This is about three small edits in workers.ts and organisations.ts and fixes the pay confidentiality and destructive-edit exposure. (b) Site scope, shared with ONB-03. Add users.siteIds (JSON array, empty means all sites) plus an optional workers.homeSiteId. Return 400 on unknown site ids at user create instead of silently dropping them. Filter shifts, eligible-workers, stats and the workers list by siteIds, and add siteIds to the POST and PATCH users schemas. Do (a) first; it is independent of (b) and is the data-protection fix.
decisionNeeded: Define the home-manager role. Option 1: rota-only, with no pay, notes or site editing, which is the safest default for delegating to home managers. Option 2: full HR for their own site only, which needs the site scope from ONB-03 plus a worker-to-site link. A related question: should pay visibility be a separate permission or flag rather than tied to the ORG_ADMIN role?

title: No expiry-horizon report: finding DBS checks expiring in 60 days means opening 413 profiles
persona: HR manager at Northern Care Group (400 staff, 8 sites); Compliance officer at Trafford Care Partnership (250 staff, surplus supplier)
evidence:
Reproduced as admin@northern-care-group.example, clock frozen at 2027-05-03T08:00Z.

API responses:
- GET /workers returns 200, 415 rows (410 ACTIVE, 5 INACTIVE), 475,007 bytes. The finding said 413.
- GET /workers?expiringWithinDays=60 returns 200 with the same 475,007 bytes, so the parameter is ignored.
- GET /workers?documentType=DBS&expiresBefore=2027-07-02 returns 200 with the same bytes, also ignored.
- GET /compliance/expiring, /reports/compliance, /workers/documents, /workers/expiring and /documents each return 404.
- GET /organisations/:id/stats has no document figures.
- docs/API.md lists only GET /workers?orgId&status&jobRole, and no document-listing endpoint (only POST/PATCH/DELETE on /workers/:id/documents).

Counts computed from the GET /workers dump:
- 17 DBS expire in the next 60 days (all on active workers). 4 expire within 30 days, and exactly those 4 are flagged EXPIRING. The 13 expiring between day 31 and day 60 show VALID/COMPLIANT.
- 38 DBS expire within 90 days.
- All document types combined: 17 mandatory training, 17 moving and handling, 20 right to work, 16 photo ID, 11 safeguarding, 9 medication, 3 NMC PIN expire within 60 days.

Code:
- apps/web/src/pages/WorkersPage.tsx (lines 14-20, 23-34): the only filters are Role and Status, passed to useWorkers({jobRole,status}). The columns are Name, Role, Skills, Status, Compliance and Shareable, so there is no expiry date column. Nothing in apps/web/src has a search box or CSV/download code.
- apps/api/src/routes/workers.ts, list handler (lines 56-76): the query schema accepts only orgId, status and jobRole, with no pagination. It computes complianceSummary for every row.
- packages/shared/src/rules/compliance.ts:32: EXPIRING_SOON_DAYS = 30. It is a global constant, not per organisation and not in platform settings. documentStatus takes an optional expiringSoonDays argument, but no caller passes it.
- apps/api/src/services/scheduler.ts:29: alertExpiringDocuments(..., horizonDays = 30) is also fixed at 30 days.
- The only place an HR manager sees an exact expiry date is WorkerDetailPage.tsx lines 55 and 106, one worker at a time. To find the 17 DBS expiries from the UI they would open up to 410 profiles, as the finding says.

Notifications (partial workaround): the latest 200 notifications for this org include 39 DOCUMENT_EXPIRING alerts mixed with 80 SHIFT_AVAILABLE and others. None of those 39 are for DBS, even though 4 DBS are inside 30 days. That may be a simulation artefact of the frozen clock, so I do not rely on it. Also raised by Compliance officer at Trafford Care Partnership (250 staff, surplus supplier): Verified against the live API at the frozen clock, logged in as the Trafford org admin. Silent filters:
- GET /workers, GET /workers?compliance=EXPIRING, GET /workers?expiringWithinDays=30 and GET /workers?bogus=1 all return 200 with the same 287,496 bytes and 250 rows.
impact: DBS renewals take weeks; a fixed 30-day flag surfaces too late, so workers silently drop out of the lendable pool (and in the UI the HR manager's only route is 413 clicks). This is routine monthly HR work that the platform cannot answer.
proposal:
Smallest sensible change, in three steps.
1. Add GET /workers/documents?type=&expiresBefore=&expiringWithinDays=&verified=&orgId=. It returns one row per document with workerId, name, role, site, type, expiresAt, verifiedAt, days remaining and status, sorted by expiry. This is one query over workerDocuments joined to workers, using the latest or best document per type, as complianceSummary already does. Paginate it (see SCL-01) and offer text/csv through the Accept header or ?format=csv (shared with REP-02).
2. Add an Expires column to the Workers page, sortable, plus a horizon filter of 30, 60 or 90 days, a document-type filter and a name search. Back it with the new endpoint, or with a nextExpiry field added to the existing /workers rows.
3. Make the expiring threshold a platform or per-organisation setting instead of the constant EXPIRING_SOON_DAYS, and have alertExpiringDocuments use the same value.

Also change parseQuery to reject unknown parameters with a 400. Silently ignoring expiringWithinDays and expiresBefore is a trap for scripts.

Fold the "upcoming expiries by month" dashboard from CMP-02, and the weekly digest from CMP-01, onto this endpoint rather than building separate queries.
decisionNeeded: Should the expiring threshold be one platform-wide default (for example 60 days) or configurable per organisation and per document type? DBS, right to work and training have different renewal lead times. Should the report cover only the organisation's own workers, or also lent-in workers whose documents the host cannot currently see?

title: Contracted hours are recorded but used by nothing: the platform cannot tell who is short of hours
persona: HR manager at Northern Care Group (400 staff, 8 sites); Rota manager at Trafford Care Partnership (surplus supplier trying to place idle staff)
evidence:
- Field is write-only. References: apps/api/src/db/schema.ts:140 (column), routes/workers.ts:25 (zod, 0-80), db/seed.ts:180 (every seeded worker gets 30), web forms in WorkersPage.tsx:60,69,93 and WorkerDetailPage.tsx:139,142,159, display only at WorkerDetailPage.tsx:41, and the sim (sim/scenario.ts:396, growth.ts, events.ts). The worker list page does not show it.
- It is absent from packages/shared/src/rules/*, packages/shared/src/dispatch/engine.ts, apps/api/src/services/eligibility.ts (lines 70-71 pass only maxHoursPerWeek and optedOutOf48h) and services/capacity.ts. The only hours input to the rule is internalHoursThisWeek (rules/eligibility.ts:38,166), which nothing sets outside a unit test.
- Live API test: 4 PATCHes (36, 0, 80, 24) each returned 200. The eligible-workers row for wrk_z4iofq54yo198ala was identical in all four (same md5, eligible:true, facts.weeklyHoursAfter:7, one OUT_OF_TRAVEL_RANGE warning). The worker is currently left at 24.
- GET /workers returns 415 rows for Northern Care Group with no booked-hours or hours-short field (keys: compliance, contractedHoursPerWeek, maxHoursPerWeek, and so on).
- Surplus flag: capacity_flags (schema.ts:187-210) has no workerId or contract link. createFlag() in services/capacity.ts writes the typed hoursRequested directly. Hours are only decremented as confirmed bookings come in (applyHoursToFlag). Nothing checks that 60h is available, or reconciles it with real contracts.
- Minor corrections to the persona's evidence: the field is also shown on the worker detail page and written by seed.ts, not only the forms and the sim. The claims about the rules, the endpoint behaviour and the flag POST are all accurate. Also raised by Rota manager at Trafford Care Partnership (surplus supplier trying to place idle staff): Checked live at http://localhost:4055 as admin@trafford-care-partnership.example, plus the source. Data and endpoints:
- GET /workers returns 250 ACTIVE workers.
impact: The premise of lending is 'staff short of hours', yet the platform treats a 24h worker exactly like a 48h one and HR has to work out surplus by hand and retype it as a flag every fortnight (see DSP-03). The field invites data entry that changes nothing.
proposal: Smallest step: add a computed hoursShort per worker (for the current week and the next four) to GET /workers. It would be max(0, contractedHoursPerWeek minus the sum of platform shifts REQUESTED, OFFERED, CONFIRMED or COMPLETED in that week), plus declared rota hours once WF-03 adds them. Show it as a sortable column with an 'org hours short' total on the worker list and the capacity page. On the Raise a flag form, pre-fill hoursRequested and jobRole for SURPLUS from the sum over shareable, active, compliant workers, and let the manager adjust it. Stretch: nudge the org when its computed surplus is above 0 and it has no active flag (this ties into DSP-03). Build it on the same weekly-hours calculation as WF-03 so both gaps use one function.
decisionNeeded: Should contracted hours only drive surplus suggestions (advisory, with the manager still typing the flag), or also cap lending, meaning no lending beyond contracted plus an allowance? And should the platform assume a worker works their full contracted hours for their employer each week unless told otherwise (the WF-03 decision), since the hours-short figure depends on that?

title: Pausing lending is one worker at a time, has no end date and no bulk or group action
persona: HR manager at Northern Care Group (400 staff, 8 sites)
evidence:
- PATCH /api/v1/workers -> 404. POST /api/v1/workers/bulk -> 404. Routes in apps/api/src/routes/workers.ts are only GET '/', POST '/', GET/PATCH '/:id', POST '/:id/login', document routes and unavailability routes.
- PATCH /workers/wrk_wa3r4e5g6afd0o1i {"shareable":false,"shareableUntil":"2027-06-03"} -> 200. The response has shareable:false and no shareableUntil key. zWorker.partial() strips the unknown key, and apps/api/src/db/schema.ts:139 has only `shareable` (bool) on workers.
- POST /workers/:id/unavailability {startsAt 2027-05-03, endsAt 2027-06-03} -> 201, one worker per call. It is the only dated mechanism and is enforced through WORKER_UNAVAILABLE in the shared eligibility rules. Cleaned up with DELETE -> 204.
- GET /workers as the Northern admin returns 415 workers (310 ACTIVE+shareable, 100 ACTIVE+non-shareable, 5 INACTIVE). The keys have no siteId or home. schema.ts:126-151 has no siteId on workers. GET /organisations/org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n/sites returns 9 sites.
- apps/web/src/pages/WorkersPage.tsx: line 18 sets role and status filters only, line 19 is the per-row toggleShare PATCH, line 48 is the per-row Toggle. The Table in apps/web/src/components/ui.tsx:262 has no selection support.
- Org-level: apps/api/src/routes/organisations.ts:38-50 PATCH accepts zOrganisation fields plus a platform-admin-only status. No lending flag exists. packages/shared/src/dispatch/engine.ts: an org without a SURPLUS flag still lands in networkEntries (about line 318).
- Enforcement: `shareable` is checked at packages/shared/src/rules/eligibility.ts (WORKER_NOT_SHAREABLE) and apps/api/src/routes/shifts.ts:475, via requestShift/offerShift only. confirmAssignment (apps/api/src/services/assignments.ts, from about line 93) has no eligibility re-check, so a REQUESTED or OFFERED assignment can still be confirmed after the worker is made non-shareable. Cancelling a CONFIRMED booking sets lateCancellation when inside settings.lateCancellationHours (24h default).
- Capacity flags can be withdrawn only one at a time (POST /capacity/flags/:id/withdraw). Northern currently has 1 ACTIVE SURPLUS flag.
- Workaround cost for the persona's task: identify the ~100 workers of the two homes (impossible from the data, because there is no site on the worker) and make ~100 PATCH or unavailability calls now. The shareable flip is then reversed by hand with ~100 more calls (or the dated unavailability windows lapse on their own), because the toggle has no end date.
impact: A one-line management decision becomes a day of clicking that must be repeated to undo and is easily forgotten, or the group lets requests happen and cancels them, which creates late-cancellation marks against the organisation.
proposal:
Smallest sensible change, in order:
1. Add nullable `workers.shareablePausedUntil` (timestamp) and make eligibility treat `now < shareablePausedUntil` as WORKER_NOT_SHAREABLE, with the date in the message. Accept `shareablePausedUntil` in the worker PATCH schema and show it on the worker list and detail. A pause then lapses by itself, with no June clean-up.
2. Add PATCH /workers/bulk (or POST /workers/bulk-update) taking {ids[], shareable?, shareablePausedUntil?}. It is org-scoped, runs in one transaction, writes one audit row per worker, and returns per-id results. Add row checkboxes, a select-all-filtered control and a "Pause lending until..." action to WorkersPage.
3. Add nullable `organisations.lendingPausedUntil`, set by an org admin in Settings. Make loadDispatchOrgs / planDispatch exclude the org with a reason such as "Organisation has paused lending until <date>", the same way status/blocked exclusions work. This covers whole-organisation pauses with no change to individual workers.
4. Follow-on, which depends on the sibling "no home site on worker" finding: add `workers.homeSiteId` and a `sites.lendingPausedUntil`. Add a site filter and site column on the Workers list, and honour the site pause in eligibility.
Also (optional, under the decision below): a "pause" action that withdraws the org's or site's active SURPLUS flags.
decisionNeeded:
When a home, group or worker is paused, what should happen to lending that is already in flight?
(a) Do nothing to existing bookings: only new requests are blocked.
(b) Also auto-withdraw REQUESTED and OFFERED (not yet CONFIRMED) assignments and notify the host.
(c) Also withdraw the organisation's or site's ACTIVE SURPLUS flags.
CONFIRMED bookings should stay and be cancelled deliberately, because cancelling them triggers late-cancellation records.
Note that today confirmAssignment does not re-check `shareable`, so (a) is not even a safe default: a host can confirm a REQUESTED assignment after the pause. At minimum confirmation should re-check the pause. Related: WF-02 for deactivated workers.
A second product question is whether the pause should be reason-coded (for example "short-staffed", "outbreak" or "CQC visit") for audit, and whether a pause should require org admin rather than manager rights.

title: The worker is shown the inter-organisation charge as their own earnings; no weekly hours total or pay status
persona: Care worker on a phone (self-service login at Riverside Living)
evidence:
1. Worker record: GET /workers/wrk_konymro0gd3gpz1d as Harry returns hourlyPayRate 12.3. This is allowed because loadWorker (apps/api/src/routes/workers.ts:84-92) treats a same-org worker as "own", so stripPrivate does not remove the field.
2. GET /timesheets returns 16 rows, ordered newest first. There are no query parameters for a date range, and the only supported filters are scope and status. I checked the code and there is no summary or total endpoint for a worker in apps/api/src/routes or docs/API.md. GET /invoices returns 403 for the worker.
3. I recomputed the over-statement with hourlyPayRate 12.30 across all 16 of Harry's timesheets:
   - "You receive" (supplierAmount) is 27% to 70% above hours x 12.30. It is 27.2% at chargeRate 17, 40.2% at 18.75, 42.1% at 19, 57.1% at 21 and 70.2% at 22.75.
   - Over all 16 rows the displayed total is £2,885.17 against £2,086.84, which is 38% too high.
   - The "£/h" shown under it is the chargeRate. That is 38% to 85% above the worker's rate.
   - The persona's "40-55%" is roughly the middle of this range, so I have corrected it to 27-70% on the amount.
4. ts_x8h583ojo1413y5f has 7.28 h at chargeRate 17. It shows "You receive £113.86" and "£17.00/h", but 7.28 x 12.30 = £89.54.
5. The persona's new timesheet ts_0xc1n4ups387wpt9 shows supplierAmount £385.96 for 22.08 h. That inflated hour count comes from the persona's own clock-in at 08:00 for a 19:00 shift and a clock-out at 07:05 the next day. The server accepts any client-supplied `at` and has no clock-in window. clockIn and clockOut in apps/api/src/services/timesheets.ts check only that the booking is live, plus clock-out after clock-in. The £385.96 is therefore not representative. At 12.30 the same 22.08 h would be £271.58.
6. Pay state: timesheet statuses are DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, DISPUTED and REJECTED (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:248). Invoice status (DRAFT, ISSUED, PAID, VOID) is organisation-level and unreadable by the worker. One APPROVED timesheet (ts_lq3p9iopmpu7io4g) has no invoiceId at all, so even the org-level state is not reliably linked.
7. Related defect found while verifying: any worker can read any colleague's hourlyPayRate and notes in the same organisation. Harry's GET /workers/wrk_yrjuztt1jbaezsfy returned 200 with hourlyPayRate 13.5 (Connor Adeyemi), and wrk_dx23oyn6r8joyz9f (Thomas Begum) returned 200 with 13.5. The cause is `own = w.orgId === user.orgId` in loadWorker, which does not distinguish role. This contradicts docs/DOMAIN-MODEL.md:22, which says the rate is private to the employer. It is a data-privacy bug (SEC-01 territory), but it bears directly on any "show pay to workers" change.
8. The WorkerDetailPage route (/workers/:id) is not in the worker's nav, but the API call works with the token.
impact: The first figure a worker sees is 40–55% above what their payslip will show; that breeds pay disputes and distrust of the platform and of the employer. Summing 15 rows by hand on a phone to answer "hours this week" is not realistic.
proposal:
Smallest sensible change, in three parts.
(a) Stop leaking the commercial charge to workers. For role WORKER, strip chargeRate, hostCost, platformFee, platformFeePct and supplierAmount from GET /timesheets and GET /timesheets/:id. Strip chargeRate from the shift payloads the worker sees (the shift board and shift detail). Change TimesheetsPage.tsx:52 and ShiftDetailPage.tsx:44 and ShiftCard.tsx:27 so a WORKER sees hours, not money. This fixes the misleading "You receive" figure whichever way the pay decision goes.
(b) Add GET /timesheets/summary?week=this|last for the worker (or a `weekSummary` block on the worker dashboard). It returns shifts, paid hours, and counts of awaiting approval, approved and disputed timesheets, plus scheduled hours for upcoming confirmed shifts so that "tonight" is answerable. Map the timesheet status to worker wording (awaiting approval, approved, queried, rejected).
(c) If the employer opts in (a single organisation setting, e.g. workerSeesEstimatedPay), return estimatedPay = paidHours x own hourlyPayRate, labelled "estimate, before tax and deductions, your payslip is the record". Fix loadWorker so a WORKER is treated as `self` only, not `own`. Today any colleague's hourlyPayRate and notes are readable. Do this in the same change, because (c) makes that field meaningful.
Not in scope: a "paid" state. Defer that to FIN-01 or a payroll export, and show approval state only until then.
decisionNeeded:
1. Should the platform show a worker any pay figure at all? Payroll is between employer and worker. Options: (i) hours and approval status only; (ii) employer opt-in estimated pay from hourlyPayRate; (iii) always on. I recommend (i) as the default with (ii) as an opt-in setting.
2. Is it acceptable to withhold the charge rate from workers entirely? That is, should the employer's margin stay confidential to managers? I assume yes.
3. What should "paid" mean for a worker? Only the employer's payroll can say, so the platform would need the employer to mark approved hours as "included in payroll run X", or a payroll export. Until that is decided, no paid state should be shown.

title: On the day: no structured "report to" or phone number, and clock-in is buried in a 15-row table and accepted 11 hours early
persona: Care worker on a phone (self-service login at Riverside Living)
evidence:
Contact:
- GET /shifts/shf_q3fgji9zwyxml31c as Harry returns site {addressLine1, city, postcode, lat, lng, accessNotes}. The notes read: "Park in the staff bays... keypad code 4471#. Report to the night senior, Ruby Ahmed, in the main office. Sign in at reception."
- The platform admin survey of /organisations/:id/sites across 22 orgs gives 35 sites, 34 with accessNotes, 33 of them the identical "Sign in at reception.", 1 naming a person (Meadow View), and 0 containing a phone number.
- GET /organisations/org_2rianfqyu0gw1u0u as Harry returns {id, name, type, serviceTypes, city, postcode, status}. The code is organisations.ts:18-37 (directoryView).
- GET /organisations as Harry returns 19 rows with the same keys, and /organisations/:id/sites returns 403 for him.

Clock:
- Persisted timesheet ts_0xc1n4ups387wpt9 shows shift 2027-05-03T19:00Z to 2027-05-04T07:00Z, clockInAt 2027-05-03T08:00Z (11 h before start), clockOutAt 2027-05-04T07:05Z, submittedAt 2027-05-03T08:00Z, status SUBMITTED, paidHours 22.08, hostCost 419.52, clockInLat/Lng null.
- The clock-out is dated about 23 h after "now" (frozen 08:00 on 3 May), so future-dated times are accepted and the timesheet is submitted 23 h before the shift ends.
- shiftPaidHours (packages/shared/src/time.ts:61) is simply (out - in) - break, with no clamp to the shift window.
- Neither clock-in nor clock-out has any time check in services/timesheets.ts (clockIn lines 61-67, clockOut 69-81). The route (routes/timesheets.ts) takes `at` as an optional zDate with no bounds.
- /submit accepts arbitrary times with breakMinutes 0-240.

UI:
- TimesheetsPage.tsx:56-57 gives every DRAFT row its own Clock in / Clock out button with no check against the shift time.
- The host's approve list shows "22.08h · £419.52" with no variance against the scheduled 11 h (DashboardPage ManagerDashboard attention list; TimesheetsPage payable tab).
- WorkerDashboard (DashboardPage.tsx:224-277) has "My upcoming shifts" (site name and postcode only) and "My timesheets". There is no today card, and the contact and map are two taps away on ShiftDetailPage.

Disclosure of arrival details:
- GET /shifts as Harry lists the Meadow View shifts shf_na5xwa4jbcv772o7, shf_gon4afaxfy0x400i and about 16 more with access.open=false, each carrying the keypad code in site.accessNotes.
impact: A worker running late has nobody to ring; a fat-finger tap on the wrong row or a too-early clock-in silently submits wrong hours the host must catch at approval, and hosts cannot treat clock times as attendance evidence.
proposal:
Smallest sensible change, in three parts.

1. Contact details.
- Add two nullable columns to sites: contactName and contactPhone. Optionally add a short entryNotes field, or keep accessNotes for that.
- Add a Settings form field for each.
- Release contactName, contactPhone and accessNotes only to a worker or supplier with a CONFIRMED assignment on that shift, in GET /shifts/:id and the scope=supplied list. Strip them from siteForGuest and the board. This also stops the keypad code reaching unreleased viewers.
- Optionally fall back to organisations.phone on a booked shift.

2. Clock validation, applied to clockIn, clockOut and submitTimes alike.
- Reject an `at` that is more than a few minutes in the future.
- Treat a clock-in earlier than startsAt minus a configurable window (default 2 h, in platform settings) as outside the window. Return a 422 unless the request carries confirmEarly: true, or accept it but store a variance flag.
- Compute and store scheduledHours against paidHours, plus an outsideWindow or variance flag. Show "Scheduled 11 h, clocked 22.08 h" on the host's Approve row, and do not auto-approve flagged timesheets.
- Geofence later, using the lat/lng already accepted.

3. UI.
- Add a "Today" card to WorkerDashboard for the next confirmed shift within about 24 h, showing address, map, contact (tap to call) and a single Clock in or Clock out button.
- Hide or disable Clock in on rows whose shift is not within the window.
decisionNeeded:
1. Are clock times attendance evidence or only a convenience for entering timesheets? If evidence, the window, future-date rejection and geofence are required and /submit must be constrained too. If convenience, a variance flag at approval is enough.
2. Who owns the on-the-day contact: a per-site field the host fills in, the host organisation's phone, or the agency or supplier manager? And should arrival details (keypad codes, names, phone) be released only once a booking is confirmed, or closer to the start time?
3. What should the default clock-in window be, and what should happen outside it: block, warn, or flag for the host?

title: No rate card: the agency cannot enforce a minimum charge rate or a night uplift, and settings silently accept unknown fields
persona: Owner of Merge Staffing (the agency that runs the platform and its own bank)
evidence:
- PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings with the minChargeRateByRole, nightUpliftPct and rateCard keys returned 200 with the body identical to GET /admin/settings (platformFeePct 8, no rate fields). apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts:22-37 uses a z.object that strips unknown keys. GET /admin/rate-card, /admin/rates and /admin/settings/rate-card all return 404.
- apps/api/src/db/schema.ts:35-53: platform_settings has platformFeePct only, with no rate card. organisations.defaultChargeRate (schema.ts:70) is a per-host suggestion, edited in apps/web/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx:60 and pre-filled at NewShiftPage.tsx:41.
- As admin@meadow-view.example, POST /api/v1/shifts with jobRole NURSE, 20:00-08:00 night, chargeRate 20 and publish true returned 201 and status OPEN. The same request with chargeRate 1 returned 201 OPEN. apps/api/src/routes/shifts.ts:33 has only positive().max(500). Both shifts were cancelled (200).
- The agency's nurses have hourlyPayRate [13,13,13,13,13,13,21] (schema.ts:148, private, never compared with chargeRate).
- Across all 1308 shifts the non-cancelled lowest nurse charge rate is £33 on days and £37 on nights, so no real undercutting has happened in the data yet.
- docs/FEATURE-ROADMAP.md:11 lists rate cards as an unbuilt feature.
impact: The agency's own nurses (bank pay rates £16-£19/h before on-costs) can be requested for £20/h shifts at a loss; hosts undercut each other on nights; and the 200 response leaves the owner believing the floor is in force when nothing changed.
proposal:
Smallest sensible slice, in two parts.
1. Make PATCH /admin/settings reject unknown keys with 400 by using .strict() on the Zod object. Consider applying the same to other write schemas.
2. Add a platform_rate_rules table or a JSON column on platform_settings with minChargeRate per job role, plus an optional night band (start/end hours and % or £ uplift). Enforce it in POST /shifts and in PATCH /shifts/:id when chargeRate is edited. Return 422 with the floor and the computed minimum, or accept with a warning flag if the owner prefers. Expose GET /admin/rate-card so the posting form can show the minimum and suggested rate. Weekend and bank-holiday bands, and a minimum supplier or worker pay rate, can follow.
decisionNeeded: Is the floor a platform-wide rule, a per-host negotiated rate card, or both? Does it hard-reject below-floor shifts or only warn? Does the night uplift raise the host's charge, the supplier's or worker's pay, or both? Should the floor apply to other suppliers' posting hosts, or only to shifts the agency's own bank can fill?

title: Suspending a non-paying host freezes its unapproved timesheets, so its debt reads £0 and its suppliers are never paid (extends PLT-01 and FIN-01)
persona: Owner of Merge Staffing (the agency that runs the platform and its own bank)
evidence:
Verified against http://localhost:4055 (clock 2027-05-03T08:00Z).

The audit log shows UPDATE organisation org_7kdf9egyq2idk5sh {status: SUSPENDED} on 2027-03-22T14:00Z by owner usr_mljuzdzyxdxuqnxe.

3. Current state is post-intervention. ts_ltw3kqogfjhe8s4m (£117.30 host cost, supplier Oakwood) and ts_dw5gjqoctu1m8kp8 (£370.26, St Anne's) are now APPROVED, with audit 'APPROVE timesheet' at 2027-05-03T08:00Z by the owner. They sit on inv_vdko0ffviznkz5hl and inv_3vskfotyirky3wce, i.e. MRG-2027-00175 and MRG-2027-00176, ISSUED, totalling £487.56. The earlier SUBMITTED state therefore rests on the audit trail plus the submit times (2026-12-17 and 2027-03-04), not on a live read. Lakeside hosted only these two timesheets in the whole dataset, so a hostOrgId=Lakeside statement count of 0 before the intervention follows.

4. Filter gap. GET /invoices?scope=all&hostOrgId=org_7kdf9egyq2idk5sh returns all 176 statements (115 PAID, 61 ISSUED); the invoices route only reads `scope` (routes/invoices.ts:21). GET /timesheets accepts only scope and status. There is no way to filter by host or counterparty in either list.

5. Missing chase and credit tooling. POST /invoices/remind, POST /organisations/org_7kdf9egyq2idk5sh/credit-hold and GET /organisations/org_7kdf9egyq2idk5sh/balance all return 404 {"error":"Not found"}. The invoices table has no dueAt (db/schema.ts:338-358), and the invoice payload carries only issuedAt and paidAt, so overdue cannot be computed. Organisation status is only PENDING, ACTIVE or SUSPENDED (routes/organisations.ts:44). There is no separate credit-hold state.

6. UI. TimesheetsPage.tsx:11 and :23 offer only payable and receivable tabs, which for a PA means the agency's own org. The useTimesheets hook already accepts 'all' (api/hooks.ts:29) and the API supports scope=all, but no screen uses it. The only on-screen signal is the 'Awaiting approval: 7 timesheets' StatCard (AdminPage.tsx:39). StatementsPage has an 'All statements' tab for the PA, but no host filter or ageing.

7. Network-wide SUBMITTED now: 7 (Meadow View, Cedar Court x1, St Anne's x1, Harmony x2, The Beeches, Sunnybank; none belong to a suspended org). Three are older than 14 days.

impact: Work done for a suspended host is never billed, other care homes that supplied the staff go unpaid, the 'what does this client owe' figure is wrong, and the debtor is locked out of the very statements it needs to pay.
proposal:
Smallest sensible slice, in order:
1. Add hostOrgId, supplierOrgId and status query filters to GET /invoices, and hostOrgId to GET /timesheets. Both are one-line zod and where additions.
2. Add an 'All hosts' tab to TimesheetsPage for platform admins (the hook and API already support scope=all), with host and age columns. Extend /admin/overview money with the £ value and oldest age of SUBMITTED timesheets. A per-host breakdown of those items could sit behind the 'Awaiting approval' card.
3. Add a credit-hold state separate from SUSPENDED (a creditHold flag on organisations, set by the PA). It blocks shift create and publish and supplier requests, but lets the org's admins still read timesheets and statements and still approve, dispute and mark-paid. Alternatively, let suspended org admins read the invoice and timesheet GETs. Do not let a suspended org's users act on any other route.
4. Add an optional platform setting `timesheetAutoApproveDays`. SUBMITTED timesheets past that age auto-approve, with a notification to host and supplier. This is shared with FIN-02.
5. Later, with FIN-01: add invoices.dueAt (issuedAt plus a payment-terms setting) and GET /organisations/:id/balance returning issued, paid and overdue by age band, plus POST /invoices/remind. A per-organisation owed figure should also count SUBMITTED-but-unapproved work as 'unbilled WIP'.
decisionNeeded: (1) Should SUBMITTED timesheets auto-approve after N days of host silence (the same decision as FIN-02), and what is N? Should a suspension also approve or settle that host's outstanding SUBMITTED items, or leave them for the PA to approve on the host's behalf? (2) Who carries credit risk when a host does not pay: the agency, which guarantees suppliers and absorbs bad debt, or the supplier, with the platform only invoicing its fee? This is the same question as FIN-01's 'who pays whom' and decides whether auto-approval is safe to enable. (3) Should a credit-hold host keep its confirmed future bookings honoured (invoiced in arrears), as PLT-01 asks, or have them cancelled?

title: Platform admin is all-or-nothing: a junior ops user sees only the agency bank, and any second admin can lock out the owner unnoticed
persona: Owner of Merge Staffing (the agency that runs the platform and its own bank)
evidence:
Throwaway accounts were created in the agency organisation org_w9x3e2yunieke54o and in Itdp Probe Care, then disabled or demoted; the real owner was not touched.

Code:
- apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts:15 gates the whole router with requireRole(PLATFORM_ADMIN).
- apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts lines 62-72 define the role sets and make assertOrgAccess pass for any platform admin.
- apps/api/src/routes/organisations.ts around lines 230-262: POST /:id/users accepts role PLATFORM_ADMIN from any platform admin into any organisation. PATCH /:id/users/:userId is open to ADMINS (platform admin and org admin) and only refuses 'cannot disable your own account'.
- The PATCH role enum is ORG_ADMIN, ORG_MANAGER or WORKER, so PLATFORM_ADMIN is rejected with 400.
- apps/web/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx:142 renders the action buttons only when u.id !== me.id and u.role !== 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'.
- ownerOrgId appears only in db/schema.ts:38, seed.ts:38, auth.ts:50 and 103, and the web types, never in authorisation.

Live calls:
- A junior ORG_MANAGER (created for the test) gets 403 on the seven admin and cross-organisation endpoints listed in the reasoning.
- An agency ORG_ADMIN gets 403 on /admin/*, /shifts?scope=all and /timesheets?scope=all, and 200 on /invoices and /organisations/<agency>/users.
- Agency ORG_ADMIN PATCH {status:DISABLED} on a test platform admin -> 200, and that admin's login then -> 401 'Account is not active'.
- Agency ORG_ADMIN PATCH {role:ORG_MANAGER} on another test platform admin -> 200, and its token then gets 403 on /admin/settings.
- Platform admin 2 PATCH /admin/settings {lateCancellationHours:24} (the default, so a no-op) -> 200. The same admin PATCH on the owner user's firstName -> 200. Self-disable -> 409.
- PATCH {role:PLATFORM_ADMIN} on a demoted admin -> 400.
- POST users with role PLATFORM_ADMIN into provider org Itdp Probe Care -> 201.
- The owner's unread count was 2444 before and after, and the audit rows were visible through GET /admin/audit.

Docs: docs/API.md line 5 describes the platform admin as a single role. Nothing in the docs or UI describes granular admin permissions or an owner flag.
impact: Every ops person who must help a client has to be given control of fees, suspensions, statements and other admins; the owner has no protection against a second admin and would not learn of a lock-out, fee change or suspension until a client phones.
proposal:
Smallest sensible fix, in three steps:

1. Protect the owner and close the escalation. Add settings.ownerUserId and have the users PATCH route refuse to disable or demote the owner except by the owner. Block non-platform-admin callers (ORG_ADMIN of the agency) from PATCHing PLATFORM_ADMIN users. Allow PLATFORM_ADMIN creation only in the agency organisation (settings.ownerOrgId). Accept PLATFORM_ADMIN in the PATCH role enum for platform-admin callers, and show Disable and Role controls for platform-admin rows in the UI, hidden for the owner row.
2. Raise a notification to every other active platform admin, and email once COM-01 lands, on platform-admin create, disable and demote, fee or setting change, and organisation suspension. Include the actor and the new value.
3. Introduce platformRole values (OWNER, OPS_READ, OPS_ACT, FINANCE) mapped to permission sets, replacing the blanket requireRole(PLATFORM_ADMIN) on admin routes. OPS_READ would cover read-only cross-organisation views, OPS_ACT would allow acting for an organisation, and FINANCE would cover invoices and fees. Add MFA or re-authentication for settings, suspension and admin-management endpoints.

Steps 1 and 2 are small, and step 1 closes the lock-out and escalation holes on its own. Step 3 is a bigger piece of work.
decisionNeeded: Which permission sets does the agency need on day one (for example owner, ops act-for-organisation, ops read-only, finance), and should sensitive actions such as fee changes, organisation suspension and disabling another admin require a second admin's approval? Should the owner be a single named user or any admin in a designated owner group? Should platform admins be restricted to the agency organisation only?

impact: The owner cannot tell which clients are profitable without a developer, and the accountant cannot be given a sales ledger, purchase ledger, bank payroll figure or VAT return from the platform; the statement as it stands is not a usable invoice.
proposal: Split it so the net-new part is cheap and the rest folds into REP-02. (1) Add a nullable workerPayRate (and optional onCostPct) column to timesheets. Copy workers.hourlyPayRate into it in createDraftTimesheet and refresh it at submit and approve until approval locks it. Backfill existing rows from the current rate, flagged as estimated. Care-home hosts often cannot reclaim VAT, so this changes what they pay. (3) Which date decides the reporting month: shift start, approval or statement period? Also confirm whether the pay-rate snapshot should include employer on-costs (NI, pension, holiday pay), since raw hourlyPayRate understates the true cost of sales.

title: Timesheets approved after the monthly run are never billed; last month's statement is silently short
persona: Finance clerk at Oakwood Care Homes (host that buys cover); Rota manager at Trafford Care Partnership (surplus supplier trying to place idle staff)
evidence:
The Oakwood figures check out. Five approved timesheets with invoiceId null have shifts before 1 May, totalling £1,018.30 (GET /timesheets?scope=payable, 200). Trafford's April statement MRG-2027-00135 (inv_fgmntfy3bawteni8, ISSUED) is £346.35 short. The code filter is shifts.startsAt in [periodStart, periodEnd) at apps/api/src/services/invoices.ts line 25. TimesheetsPage.tsx and StatementsPage.tsx show no unbilled bucket, and GenerateModal defaults to the current month (StatementsPage.tsx lines 85-87). Network-wide (platform admin, scope=all, 200): 53 timesheets / £11,685.55 host cost / £934.80 fee, oldest ts_nhtt8dyn483igh54 (shift 2026-11-30, approved 2026-12-01 14:00, almost five months unbilled). 44 were approved 0 to 3.4 days after the run; 9 fell into the 08:00Z boundary gap. Workaround: POST /invoices/generate for the past period issues a supplementary statement. I did not run it, to avoid altering shared data. Also raised by Rota manager at Trafford Care Partnership (surplus supplier trying to place idle staff): All figures were checked against the live API. Access as the Trafford rota manager (rota@trafford-care-partnership.example):
- GET /invoices, /invoices?scope=receivable and /invoices/:id return 403 (ADMINS only in apps/api/src/routes/invoices.ts).

proposal:
Smallest fix has two parts.
1. Drop the lower bound by default. In generateInvoices, select approved, un-invoiced timesheets with shifts.startsAt < periodEnd, or add an includePriorPeriods flag the monthly run and Generate modal turn on. Late approvals then land on the next statement. The line already carries the shift date, which the drawer should show per line, labelled "prior period" where it applies.
2. Show the gap. Add an "Approved, not yet on a statement" count and £ total (GET /invoices/unbilled, or a summary on GET /invoices) as a banner on the Statements page for hosts and suppliers. Add a "Statement" column to the Timesheets page showing the invoice number or "not yet billed". Make the Generate modal's result and default list what it will pick up.
decisionNeeded: Is a statement period defined by when the work happened (shift date) or when it was approved? This decides whether late approvals go on the next statement as clearly labelled prior-period lines, or on a supplementary statement re-issued for the original period. It affects how suppliers reconcile against their own records and which month's accruals the host books the cost to. Related: should the monthly run be automatic or stay a manual "Generate statements" action?

title: 'Paid' is a one-sided flag either party can set, with no reference, no notification and no trail the host can see
persona: Finance clerk at Oakwood Care Homes (host that buys cover)
evidence:
VERIFIED by code and live API (http://localhost:4055, logged in as the Oakwood, Northern Care Group and platform admins).

1. Either party can mark paid. apps/api/src/routes/invoices.ts lines 81-95 (POST /invoices/:id/mark-paid, requireRole(ADMINS)) looks the statement up where hostOrgId = my org OR supplierOrgId = my org, and platform admin can mark any statement. It sets only status=PAID and paidAt=now(). apps/web/src/pages/StatementsPage.tsx line 41 shows a "Mark paid" button on every ISSUED row, on both the Payable and Receivable tabs. docs/API.md line 98 lists it simply as OA/PA.

2. No payment record. The invoices table (apps/api/src/db/schema.ts lines 338-358) has the statement amounts (subtotal, platformFee, supplierAmount, totalHours) plus status, issuedAt and paidAt. It has no paid amount, payment method, reference, payer or marked-by field. The statement drawer (StatementsPage.tsx line 59) shows only "Paid: <date>". GET /invoices/inv_uoedeb8rlze7oln8 as Oakwood returns status PAID, paidAt 2027-05-03T08:00:00Z and nothing about who set it.

3. No notification. mark-paid receives only { db, now } from deps (no notifier). NotificationType (packages/shared/src/enums.ts around lines 271-287) has INVOICE_ISSUED but no paid or payment type. Oakwood's notifications by type are INVOICE_ISSUED 13, SHIFT_AVAILABLE 10, DOCUMENT_EXPIRING 8, SHIFT_REQUEST 6, TIMESHEET_SUBMITTED 5, TIMESHEET_APPROVED 3, SHIFT_DECLINED 3, SHIFT_UNFILLED 2, with nothing about payment. The latest INVOICE_ISSUED is MRG-2027-00175 (the finding's "latest is INVOICE_ISSUED" is only true when filtering to invoice types, because the unread feed is dominated by shift notifications).

4. Audit trail not visible to the parties. GET /admin/audit?entityType=invoice&entityId=inv_uoedeb8rlze7oln8 returns 403 for both the Oakwood org admin and the Northern Care Group org admin. It works for the platform admin (200). Its two rows are CREATE 2027-05-01 and UPDATE {paid:true} 2027-05-03 with actorUserId usr_uz6sty3qe1kimc0u and actorOrgId org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n (Northern Care Group, the supplier). Across all 291 invoice audit rows (176 CREATE, 115 paid), 0 have a null actor, which contradicts the stated "actorUserId null".

5. Cannot be undone. Re-posting mark-paid on the already-PAID statement as Oakwood returns 409 {"error":"Statement is paid"}. Only ISSUED can become PAID, and the code has no route that voids, reopens or disputes a statement. InvoiceStatus defines DRAFT and VOID but nothing sets them. A supplier or host who marks one by mistake cannot correct it.

6. State checks. GET /invoices?scope=payable as Oakwood returns 34 statements. The 9 April statements are MRG-2027-00135, 136, 137, 147, 150, 151, 159, 163 and 169; 8 are ISSUED and 137 is now PAID because of the persona's test. March statements are PAID with paidAt 2027-04-13T10:00Z, and the March MRG-2027-00112 paid row was marked by Oakwood's own admin. So the clerk can check state, but the platform cannot prove payment or tell the clerk who marked what.
impact: The clerk cannot produce a remittance, payment date or payer identity to a supplier who disputes payment, cannot tell that a PAID flag was set by the other side, and a supplier can close its own receivable (or a host its payable) by mistake or on purpose.
proposal:
Smallest sensible change, in three steps.
(a) Add a payment record. Add paidBy (user and org id), paymentMethod and paymentReference columns, plus a paidAmount that defaults to the statement subtotal, to the invoice or a small payments table. Have mark-paid accept optional method, reference and date, and store who marked it. Show these in the statement drawer and in GET /invoices/:id, together with a payment history that lists the matching audit entries.
(b) Notify the counterparty. Add a NotificationType INVOICE_PAID that mark-paid sends to the other party. Add an "I haven't received this" action that moves the statement to a DISPUTED state (an extra InvoiceStatus value) or reopens it to ISSUED, so a wrong flag can be corrected. Add a platform-admin or payee-confirmed void path.
(c) Make the audit readable. Give each party read access to the audit rows for statements they are party to, for example GET /invoices/:id/history, rather than opening /admin/audit.
Optionally restrict who may mark a statement paid (see the decision below).
decisionNeeded: Who is allowed to record payment: (1) only the payer (host), with the payee confirming receipt or disputing it, both notified; (2) either party, as today, but with the marker recorded, the counterparty notified, and the flag reversible; or (3) capture automatically from a collection provider (roadmap item 4 and FIN-01), after which the manual flag becomes an exception route. This depends on the FIN-01 decision on who pays whom. If hosts pay the platform and the platform pays suppliers, only the platform should set PAID. If hosts pay suppliers directly, the host records payment and the supplier confirms it.

evidence:

Also expose siteId and siteName on the line in GET /invoices/:id. This is small, needs no new decisions, and removes most of the re-keying. title: No budget controls: no spend cap per site, no sign-off above a rate, and spend by site needs a client-side join
persona: Finance clerk at Oakwood Care Homes (host that buys cover)
evidence:
Reproduced as admin@oakwood-care-homes.example (org_fjm12vutd7b8xabi).

Budget and limit fields
- No budget or limit field exists. The sites table in apps/api/src/db/schema.ts (lines 95-111) has only id, orgId, name, serviceType, address, lat/lng, accessNotes and createdAt.
- A grep for budget, spendLimit or signOff across apps and docs matches only docs/FEATURE-ROADMAP.md:40.
- GET /organisations/:id/sites/:siteId/budget returns 404.
- PATCH /organisations/:id with {"monthlySpendLimit":5000} returns 200 and the field is silently dropped.
- PATCH .../sites/site_0yul6o0nxd3warhb with {"monthlyBudget":5000} returns 500 "Internal server error".
- PATCH .../sites/site_0yul6o0nxd3warhb with {} also returns 500.
- PATCH .../sites/site_0yul6o0nxd3warhb with {"accessNotes":"...","monthlyBudget":5000} returns 200 with monthlyBudget silently ignored.
- Cause: organisations.ts lines 136-137 run `db.update(sites).set(body)` with an empty body after zod strips the unknown key. {"name":""} correctly returns 400.

Rate control
- apps/api/src/routes/shifts.ts line 33 validates chargeRate only as `z.number().positive().max(500)`. The edit path (line 283) only re-notifies on a rate rise. Nothing holds, approves or flags a high rate.
- apps/web/src/pages/NewShiftPage.tsx defaults chargeRate to organisation.defaultChargeRate (£17 for Oakwood). Line 158 is a plain number input with no warning or threshold, and "Publish now" (line 178) publishes immediately.
- Of the 177 shifts Oakwood has posted (GET /shifts?scope=posted&includePast=true), 131 are above the £17 default and 17 are at £33. The highest is £44.25.
- Five approved April timesheets are at £33 or above, and all five are invoiced. The April statements MRG-2027-00137 (PAID), -00147 and -00150 contain £33 lines, with no approval step before they were committed.

Spend by site
- GET /organisations/:id/stats returns an identical payload with or without from/to/groupBy (periodDays 30, approvedSpend 7238.63). The route is organisations.ts lines 54-85, with a hard-coded `since = addDays(at, -30)`.
- DashboardPage.tsx line 40 shows only that single "Approved spend" tile.
- Timesheet rows carry shiftId, hostCost and approvedAt but no siteId. Invoice lines are the same: GET /invoices/:id lines[] carry shiftId and a shift stub with {id, title, jobRole, startsAt, endsAt} and no siteId.
- GET /timesheets?scope=payable&siteId=... returns 200 with all 153 rows, so the filter is silently ignored. The query schema (timesheets.ts line 34) accepts only scope and status.
- The client-side join works: timesheets (153 rows) + shifts (177 rows here, 171 in the finding) + sites, with shift start month as the month key. It reproduces the finding's figures exactly:
  - Altrincham: Feb 3,046.89, Mar 2,189.16, Apr 3,015.13.
  - Manchester: Feb 1,659.20, Mar 1,292.47, Apr 3,662.69.
- Grouping by approvedAt month instead gives different totals (Altrincham Apr 2,882.53, Manchester Apr 3,448.94), so even the month basis is ambiguous without a defined rule.
impact: A rota manager can commit any amount at any rate and finance only sees it after approval; monthly spend per home cannot be tracked against a budget without a spreadsheet built from three API dumps.
proposal:
Smallest sensible slice, in three parts.
1. Fix the data model. Add siteId to timesheets (denormalised from the shift at creation, with a backfill) and expose it on timesheet rows and invoice lines. Accept siteId, from and to filters on GET /timesheets and GET /invoices. Add `groupBy=site|supplier|month` and `from`/`to` to the org stats endpoint, and show a spend-by-site table with date range on the dashboard. Coordinate with REP-02 so this is one piece of work.
2. Add the controls. Add nullable `monthlyBudget` to sites and nullable `rateApprovalThreshold` to organisations, editable in Settings. title: No way to record a safeguarding concern about a lent worker, and nothing tells anyone it happened

evidence:

NotificationType (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:271-286) has no concern or safeguarding type. I scanned the first 50 notifications for the platform admin, Trafford and Oakwood.    - POST /assignments/:id/rating {score 1-5, comment} (assignments.ts:176-195) stores the comment, but no endpoint or page returns it. Only the average score is read (workers.ts:115,123; shifts.ts:405). The route sends no notification. A re-rating deletes the previous one (assignments.ts:189). So the supplier never sees the host's comment, which is stronger than the persona said.
   - POST /assignments/:id/no-show does notify the supplier (services/assignments.ts:251), but it records non-attendance, not a safeguarding concern, and needs a booking in CONFIRMED status.
   - PUT /organisations/:id/relationships/:otherOrgId {kind: BLOCKED} is org-wide. It is applied only in dispatch tiering (packages/shared/src/dispatch/engine.ts:238-243), so it hits every Trafford worker, not one person or one site.

impact: A CQC-regulated supplier lending 250 staff to 18 hosts has no auditable record of an allegation, no link from the concern to the shift and host, no protected hold, and no way for the host to report it in the first place. The record it does have can be overwritten by anyone editing the profile. A compliance officer cannot sign off lending at scale on this basis.
proposal:
Smallest useful step is a new concerns table and routes. Attachments, a per-site do-not-return marker and mediation come later.

1. Tables: `concerns` (id, workerId, assignmentId nullable, raisedByOrgId, raisedByUserId, category, summary, status OPEN/INVESTIGATING/CLOSED, outcome, createdAt, closedAt) and an append-only `concern_notes` table (no UPDATE or DELETE).
2. Routes:
   - POST /assignments/:id/concerns, for host or supplier managers, derives the worker, shift and host from the booking.
   - POST /workers/:id/concerns, for the supplier only.
   - GET /concerns, scoped so the supplier sees concerns about its workers, the host sees those it raised, and the platform admin sees all.
   - POST /concerns/:id/notes and PATCH /concerns/:id for status and outcome.
3. Hold: opening a concern sets a hold on the worker. Add a WORKER_ON_HOLD eligibility blocker, separate from shareable and independent of the checkbox. Only closing the concern, or the platform admin, lifts it. Withdraw or flag future CONFIRMED and REQUESTED assignments for that worker (shares the fix with WF-02).
4. Notifications: add NotificationType.SAFEGUARDING_CONCERN, sent immediately to supplier org admins and the platform admin.
5. Visibility: let the supplier's org admin read the audit trail for its own workers.
6. Quick wins in the meantime:
   - Return the rating comment to the counterparty and notify on a low score.
   - Make worker.notes append-only, or show its history.
decisionNeeded:
- Who sees a concern raised by a host: only the supplier and the platform, or (anonymised) other hosts?
- Does the platform mediate, or is it supplier-only?
- Who may lift a hold: the supplier's org admin, or only the platform admin?
- Does the worker get notice and a right of reply?
- Legal handling of allegation data about a named individual (retention, access rights, referrals to the regulator, DBS or local authority). This ties into SEC-01.

title: A manager cannot bar one worker from the home, and blocking their whole employer does not cover shifts already posted
persona: Registered manager facing a CQC inspection at Northern Care Group, Didsbury home
evidence:
I checked each claim against the running API and the code.

A. No per-worker block.
- PUT /organisations/{NCG}/relationships/wrk_konymro0gd3gpz1d returned 404 "Organisation not found".
- POST /workers/{id}/block returned 404 "Not found".
- grep of apps, packages and docs finds no worker-level bar anywhere. The eligibility blocker codes in packages/shared/src/rules/eligibility.ts have none for a host-side bar: SHIFT_IN_PAST, OWN_ORGANISATION, WORKER_INACTIVE, WORKER_NOT_SHAREABLE, ROLE_MISMATCH, MISSING_SKILLS, NON_COMPLIANT, NO_ACCESS, ACCESS_NOT_OPEN, WORKER_UNAVAILABLE, OVERLAPPING_SHIFT, INSUFFICIENT_REST, WEEKLY_HOURS_EXCEEDED and SHIFT_TOO_LONG.
- Ratings play no part in eligibility, so the 1-star score has no effect.

B. Silent field drop.
- PUT .../relationships/{Riverside} with {kind:BLOCKED, workerId, siteId, note} returned 200 and echoed only {orgId, otherOrgId, kind, note}.
- The route in apps/api/src/routes/organisations.ts (about line 183) uses a plain z.object, which strips unknown keys. The block is organisation-wide, at every Northern site.

C. Role.
- The rota manager (ORG_MANAGER) got 403 on the same PUT.
- The route uses requireRole(...ADMINS) = PLATFORM_ADMIN and ORG_ADMIN only (apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts line 63).
- docs/API.md line 25 documents this.

D. Block not enforced on open shifts. I reproduced this live and cleaned up afterwards.
- I published an urgent auto-confirm Didsbury shift (shf_8yiggpc76eapi34g, CARE_ASSISTANT, starts 2027-05-03T20:00Z). The shift_access row for Riverside opened at 08:00 (NETWORK tier).
- I blocked Riverside with PUT .../relationships/{Riverside}.
- Afterwards, GET /shifts/:id as Riverside returned 200 with access.open=true.
- The host's own plan view still listed Riverside Living.
- POST /shifts/:id/requests as the Riverside admin for worker wrk_pm9fhoiea19s3jk0 returned 201 with a CONFIRMED assignment (asg_3o1ja7ifh107asac), because autoConfirm was on.
- Cause: accessFor() (apps/api/src/services/dispatch.ts lines 147-151) reads only the shift_access row. It never checks org_relationships. Blocks are applied only inside planDispatch (packages/shared/src/dispatch/engine.ts lines 238-245) when a plan is built, which happens at publish time. replanOpenShiftsForOrg is called only from services/capacity.ts line 49, for surplus flags, and it only adds or promotes access. Nothing removes access after a block.
- Both requestShift and offerShift go through evaluateWorkerForShift, which uses accessFor, so both are exposed. GET /shifts/:id/candidates reads shift_access rows directly, so it is exposed in the same way.

E. Misleading banner.
- apps/web/src/pages/NetworkPage.tsx line 23 says "Blocked organisations never see your shifts and you never see theirs". That is not true for shifts open at block time.

Cleanup done: I cleared the Riverside block and cancelled my two test shifts (shf_py7lbri9r0gd04js and shf_8yiggpc76eapi34g). The test booking was auto-cancelled. The relationships list is back to the original single Trafford block ("2 no-shows"). Neither of my test shifts can be deleted, so they remain as CANCELLED rows.
impact: After a safeguarding concern, a registered manager cannot give an inspector a reliable "this person will not be sent here again". The only control removes every worker from that supplier, sits with the org admin rather than the home's manager, and lets the barred supplier keep booking, even auto-confirmed, onto any shift that was open when the block was made. This extends TRS-01 (which is about confirmed bookings and reliability scores): here, new bookings get through after a block.
proposal:
Smallest sensible fix, in two parts.

1. Make the organisation block real. Add a relationship check to accessFor, or to evaluateWorkerForShift, so a blocked organisation, in either direction, gets NO_ACCESS immediately. Better still, on PUT relationships with kind=BLOCKED, delete that organisation's shift_access rows for the host's open shifts. Return the number of live bookings still in place with that organisation so the UI can prompt, which also covers the TRS-01 prompt. Correct the NetworkPage banner.

2. Add a per-worker "do not return" record: new table worker_bars (hostOrgId, optional siteId, workerId, reason, setByUserId, createdAt, optional reviewAt).
- Enforce it in evaluateEligibility as a WORKER_BARRED blocker, on both requests and offers. Also filter barred workers out of /candidates.
- Let ORG_MANAGERs set bars for sites they manage. Keep organisation blocks admin-only.
- Show the supplier that the worker is barred. Show the reason only if the host chooses to share it.
- Include the bars in the host's audit log and the REP-01 inspector export.

Also make parseBody strict, or reject unknown keys on this route, so workerId and siteId return a 400 and are not dropped silently.
decisionNeeded: Should a worker bar apply to one site or the whole host group by default? Should the platform/agency be told, or mediate, when the reason is safeguarding? Should a bar also cancel the worker's existing future bookings with the host, or only prevent new ones? Should organisation blocks stay admin-only while worker bars go to site managers?

title: Feedback on borrowed workers goes nowhere: rating comments can never be read back, the supplier is not told, and there is no incident record
persona: Registered manager facing a CQC inspection at Northern Care Group, Didsbury home
evidence: Live API at localhost:4055: GET /incidents, /complaints, /feedback, /ratings, /concerns all return 404. Link it to TRS-01 so an upheld incident can count against the worker's reliability record or set a do-not-return marker.
decisionNeeded: Who can see an incident: only the host and the worker's employer, or also the platform and agency staff and other hosts who use the same worker? Is the worker entitled to see it and reply (data-protection access rights)? What must be passed on by law when the concern is safeguarding (local authority referral, CQC notification, employer's duty to refer to the DBS), and does the platform only record that it was reported or also help send the report? Who decides the outcome when host and supplier disagree: the platform or each side?

impact: The inspector asks how the home managed gaps in staffing. The platform can show a gap happened, but not that it was sent out to 17 organisations, escalated, or covered internally. That evidence is exactly what was deleted. Partly filled shifts look as if they were covered.

Three small steps, in order.
1. Stop deleting shift_access rows in cancelShift (shifts.ts:46) and progressShifts (shifts.ts:68). Add a closedAt (or closedReason) column instead. Add a status check to GET /shifts/:id/candidates so retained rows do not offer candidates on past shifts. Show the ReleasePlan card on ShiftDetailPage for every status (line 79), titled "Release history" for past shifts. Allow a host-only PATCH or POST /shifts/:id/outcome on EXPIRED, COMPLETED and CANCELLED shifts where filledCount < headcount, writing an audit row (action OUTCOME). Show a "needs outcome" badge on posted shifts, and send SHIFT_UNFILLED (or a new SHORT_STAFFED type) when a shift starts with filledCount < headcount, not only when it is 0.

decisionNeeded: Should a supplier organisation that was in a past shift's plan still be able to open that shift (GET /shifts/:id via accessFor) once the rows are retained, or should closed rows be hidden from supplier-side access? evidence:

Median 42 h, min 6 h, max 156 h, measured from request to shift start. About 1,536 gross hours, about £32.1k gross before breaks. Spread over 54 distinct workers.

Per host (requested, confirmed, unanswered): Meadow View 44/0/44, Elm Tree Care 27/0/27, Lakeside Lodge 17/0/17, Sunnybank 18/0/17, Birch House 5/0/5, Willow Homecare 5/0/5, Bright Horizons 3/0/3. Code references:
- apps/api/src/services/eligibility.ts:18 and :40: LIVE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES includes REQUESTED and feeds bookedShifts.
- packages/shared/src/rules/eligibility.ts:158: the OVERLAPPING_SHIFT blocker.
- apps/api/src/services/shifts.ts:59: progressShifts closes pending requests only once the shift has started.
- apps/api/src/services/shifts.ts, warnUnfilledSoon: the warning text mentions rate, visibility and the agency bank, and no waiting requests.
- apps/api/src/services/assignments.ts, withdrawRequest, and the POST /:id/withdraw route in apps/api/src/routes/assignments.ts: manual release exists.
- apps/api/src/services/assignments.ts, confirmAssignment: it does no eligibility or overlap re-check on confirm.
- apps/api/src/routes/shifts.ts, GET / available scope: returns only hostName and site, with no host stats.

Live test: POST /shifts/shf_o1uvdif7oaheqoul/requests for wrk_27ajujjwlyqwfi31 returned 201 REQUESTED. Admin eligible-workers on shf_p1zsb1lpayo5qy06 with orgId set to Trafford then showed OVERLAPPING_SHIFT. POST /assignments/asg_6xjtfjn61ye5u942/withdraw returned 200 WITHDRAWN and the blocker vanished.
impact: Idle staff are held on requests that will never be answered. Meanwhile they cannot be sent to hosts that would confirm them. The supplier cannot tell the two kinds of host apart, so it keeps putting staff forward to hosts that never answer. Hosts let shifts expire unfilled while willing, eligible workers wait. Both sides lose revenue, and suppliers lose trust in the exchange.
proposal:
Smallest sensible slice, in priority order.

1. Show host responsiveness to suppliers. Compute, per host organisation over a trailing 60-90 days, requestsReceived, confirmationRatePct and medianHoursToRespond. Return it as hostStats on GET /shifts?scope=available and GET /shifts/:id, and render it on ShiftCard and the board as a small badge such as "Confirms 4 in 5 requests, typically within 3 h" or "Rarely answers". Include it in the put-forward list too. This is a read-only aggregation over shift_assignments and needs no schema change.

2. Make an unanswered REQUESTED a soft hold. Either:
   - (a) Auto-expire a REQUESTED assignment after a set age, or at X hours before the start if that is earlier. Mark it DECLINED or EXPIRED with the note 'No response from host', notify the supplier, and treat that as a host non-response in the stats. Or:
   - (b) Stop counting REQUESTED toward OVERLAPPING_SHIFT for new requests and keep only CONFIRMED and OFFERED as firm time. If you do this, add an eligibility or overlap re-check inside confirmAssignment, which has none today, and auto-withdraw the worker's other overlapping REQUESTED rows when one is confirmed (first confirm wins).
   - Also add a per-request "release if another shift confirms" option as the cheap variant.

3. Make the host's 24 h unfilled warning (warnUnfilledSoon) list the pending requests, with deep links to Confirm. This is a few lines of body text.

4. Defer host-level auto-confirm and consequences for persistently unresponsive hosts, and fold that into DSP-02's auto-confirm policy. An organisation-level "instant book by default" setting is the cheapest step, since instant book is currently per shift only.
decisionNeeded: How long may an unanswered request hold a worker before it lapses: a fixed number of hours after the request, or a point before the shift start (for example 12 h after, or 24 h before)? Should the hold be soft (a firm booking elsewhere wins, first confirm wins) or should the platform keep blocking and just auto-release? And what, if anything, should happen to a host that persistently ignores requests: only show the stat, rank its shifts lower on the board, prompt it to switch on instant book, or eventually pause its shifts?
