- GET /shifts/shf_o1uvdif7oaheqoul/eligible-workers lists wrk_9vff as eligible:true, blockers [], with only an OUT_OF_TRAVEL_RANGE warning (30.5km vs a 25km limit). Of 250 workers, 181 are eligible and 195 carry the distance warning. No parking or site-exclusion signal exists.
- GET /shifts?scope=available returned 26 shifts. The supplier sees site.accessNotes on each. This is the only place parking text reaches them, and only after release.
- evaluateWorkerForShift (apps/api/src/services/eligibility.ts) feeds the shared evaluateEligibility. It has no site-facility or worker-condition inputs. Both requestShift and offerShift use it, so a worker's self-request on the board is not checked either.
- A worker PATCH on their own record (daniel.hussain.141@... with Temp-Pass-1234) returned 403, so workers cannot record conditions either.
- docs/FEATURE-ROADMAP.md line 45 mentions site packs (parking) only as an in-app messaging idea, not as structured matching.
impact: Workers' practical conditions get lost. The result is refused or abandoned shifts, avoidable late cancellations, and staff who stop taking shifts through the platform. The more staff a supplier has, the harder these conditions are to keep in a manager's head.
proposal:
Smallest useful slice, in two parts.
1. Add a small structured conditions record on sites and workers.
   - Sites: a few boolean or enum facility flags (staffParking, stepFreeAccess, publicTransportNearby), editable in SettingsPage.tsx next to Access notes. Expose them in siteForGuest.
   - Workers: requiresParking, an optional excludedHostOrgIds / excludedSiteIds list, and an optional maxTravelMinutes. Keep the existing travelRadiusKm. Allow the worker's own manager, and ideally the worker via self-service, to edit them. Add the fields to zWorker and the WorkerDetailPage form.
2. Feed the conditions into evaluateEligibility as new warning codes (for example NEEDS_PARKING_NOT_AVAILABLE, EXCLUDED_SITE). It already carries warnings such as OUT_OF_TRAVEL_RANGE. Show them in eligible-workers, the put-forward flow, host offers, and the worker's own board.

Do not add an automatic hard block in v1. The dispatch engine's BLOCKED relationship stays org-level only.
decisionNeeded: Which site facilities to standardise. Whether worker conditions are hard blockers or warnings that a manager can override. Whether a worker can edit their own conditions or only their employer can. Also whether the distance warning, which already fires for 195 of 250 workers on the sampled shift, should be tightened first so a new warning does not add to the noise.

title: Open sign-up gives an unchecked stranger care-home addresses and staff door codes in three calls
persona: IT and data-protection lead evaluating Merge for a provider group
evidence:
Checked live at http://localhost:4055 and in the code.

1. Unauthenticated GET /organisations, /workers, /shifts, /capacity/network and /auth/me all return 401. That is correct behaviour.

2. POST /auth/register needs no auth and returned 201 with organisation.status ACTIVE plus an ORG_ADMIN token.
   - The code is at apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts, lines 56-69. It hard-codes status:'ACTIVE' at line 66.
   - The password "password" was accepted. zAdmin only requires min(8) characters, with no strength check.
   - cqcRegistrationNumber is nullable and optional (auth.ts line 17). My probe registered without one.
   - No rate limit exists. A grep for rateLimit, express-rate and helmet in apps/api/src finds nothing.

3. Before any flag, the new organisation's GET /shifts?scope=available returned 0 rows. After POST /capacity/flags {kind:SURPLUS, jobRole:CARE_ASSISTANT, hoursRequested:10, radiusKm:80}, which returned 201, the same call returned 26 Meadow View rows.
   - In my run 3 were PRIORITY and already open, and 23 were NETWORK and not yet open. The original count of 8 and 18 differs only because of the flag window.
   - All 26 rows carried site.addressLine1 "28 Church Road", postcode WN1 4AB and lat/lng. All 26 also carried accessNotes with the "Staff door keypad code 4471#" text and "Report to the night senior, Ruby Ahmed".
   - Cause: apps/api/src/routes/shifts.ts line 216 defines siteForGuest(), which includes addressLine1, lat, lng and accessNotes unconditionally. It is applied at line 174 for scope=available, line 144 for scope=supplied, and line 250 for GET /shifts/:id for any organisation that has access.
   - No check is made for a CONFIRMED assignment. ShiftDetailPage.tsx lines 61-64 renders the notes. SettingsPage.tsx line 86 promises "Access notes are shared with confirmed workers."

4. The same leak affects legitimate members. admin@riverside-living.example sees accessNotes on 26 of 26 available rows, and 25 of those are not yet open to Riverside.

5. Email enumeration: POST /auth/register with harry.mensah.730@riverside-living.example and with admin@northern-care-group.example returned 409 "An account with that email already exists" (auth.ts line 62). The 409 is returned before any row is inserted, so enumeration is free and side-effect-free. There is no rate limit.

6. Demo box: apps/web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx lines 6-13 and 58-70 render it unconditionally, with the password password123. apps/web/src uses no import.meta.env gate. seed.ts lines 21 and 45 create admin@merge.local as PLATFORM_ADMIN with that password. On this instance admin@merge.local with password123 returns 401, so this is a deployment risk only.

7. PENDING exists as an OrgStatus. PATCH /organisations/:id accepts status PENDING (organisations.ts line 44). packages/shared/src/dispatch/engine.ts line 234 excludes non-ACTIVE organisations from dispatch. lib/auth.ts line 47 blocks only SUSPENDED organisations, so a PENDING organisation could still log in.

Cleanup: I withdrew my probe flag (flag_rd29zspetswvqshd, 200). I suspended my probe organisation org_91ucc6esyhjt49fh (200), and its token now gets 403 "Your organisation is suspended". The earlier probe organisation was already suspended.
impact: Anyone on the internet can, within seconds, learn where vulnerable residents live, how to get in through the staff door and whom to ask for. A data-protection lead cannot accept that. It also turns the shift board into a reconnaissance tool and lets an attacker confirm which staff emails to target for phishing.
proposal:
Smallest sensible change, in priority order.

1. Register creates the organisation as PENDING. A platform admin approves it by setting status ACTIVE through the existing PATCH /organisations/:id. The engine already skips non-ACTIVE organisations. Also make lib/auth.ts block a PENDING organisation from posting shifts or raising flags until it is approved. Show a "waiting for approval" screen. Make the CQC number mandatory at registration, and add a minimum password strength rule. Add a rate limit on /auth/register and /auth/login.

2. Split the site payload. siteForGuest should return only name, serviceType, city and postcode area, with lat/lng coarsened or rounded to about 1 km.
   - Return the full addressLine1, exact lat/lng and accessNotes only when the viewer is the host, a platform admin, or the supplier or worker holds a CONFIRMED assignment on that shift.
   - Apply this to scope=available, scope=supplied and GET /shifts/:id.
   - Optionally release the full address once the viewer's tier is open and a request is made, but never before.
   - Update the ShiftDetailPage block that shows access notes so it shows them only when an assignment is confirmed.

3. Make register respond the same whether or not the email exists, for example 202 "check your email", or collapse into the approval flow from item 1.

4. Gate the demo-login box with import.meta.env.DEV, and remove the seeded demo accounts from production seeding.

5. Add a hint on the Sites access-notes field: "Do not store door codes here; give them to confirmed workers directly."
decisionNeeded: What checks must a new organisation pass before it joins the network and sees any shifts or site details? The options are a CQC registration check, a signed data-sharing or data-processing agreement, and manual approval by the operator. Who carries out those checks and who owns the approval queue? Separately, should the precise address be shown before a worker is confirmed, and what is the policy for door codes: are they shared only inside the platform after confirmation, or kept out of the platform entirely?

title: The agency's admin login can read every provider's pay rates, DBS numbers and private notes, and nothing records it
persona: IT and data-protection lead evaluating Merge for a provider group
evidence:
Checked on the running platform (clock 2027-05-03).

Platform admin (owner@merge-staffing.example, PLATFORM_ADMIN):
- GET /workers returned 200 with 1371 workers across 21 organisations. hourlyPayRate was non-null for 1367. The finding's 1369 and 1366 are slightly off; the point stands.
- GET /workers/wrk_dhks6qtspa31pssb (org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n, a Northern Care worker) returned 200 with hourlyPayRate 12.5 and a documents[] array. The DBS entry has reference "DBS-Femi", issuedAt, expiresAt and verifiedAt. The notes field is returned but is null for this worker. Only 1 of the 1371 workers has non-null notes in the seed data.
- Also 200 for GET /workers?orgId=org_w9x3e2yunieke54o, GET /organisations/org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n/users, GET /organisations/org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n/sites and GET /invoices?scope=all.
- Merge Staffing is type AGENCY and has the single PLATFORM_ADMIN user (owner@). Its other users (dana.ops-lead, jo.junior and others) are ORG_MANAGER or ORG_ADMIN, and its bank workers are WORKER logins.
- GET /admin/audit?limit=500 returned 200, with 500 rows holding LOGIN, UPDATE, CREATE, DELETE, APPROVE, CANCEL, PUBLISH, REQUEST, WITHDRAW and CONFIRM. There is no read action, and no worker read or document read appears.

Code:
- stripPrivate is at workers.ts:45-49. The own flag is computed at workers.ts:66 (list), workers.ts:94 (loadWorker) and workers.ts:118.
- AuditAction is at packages/shared/src/enums.ts:289-303 (CREATE through LOGIN, no VIEW).
- The audit route is at apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts:87-101, behind adminRouter.use(requireAuth, requireRole(PLATFORM_ADMIN)) at admin.ts:15.
- The only audit UI is the platform admin's AdminPage.tsx 'Audit log' tab.
- Document `reference` is sent whole in GET /workers/:id (workers.ts:106 and 118) and is shown in WorkerDetailPage.tsx:104.

Tenant side (rota@northern-care-group.example, ORG_MANAGER):
- GET /workers returned 415 workers, all in its own organisation (the finding says 414), of which 412 have hourlyPayRate and 0 have notes.
- GET /workers/:id returned pay 12.5 and the DBS reference "DBS-Femi".
- GET /admin/audit returned 403, and it also returned 403 for admin@northern-care-group.example (ORG_ADMIN), so tenants have no audit view at all.
- A worker from another organisation returned 403 "That worker belongs to another organisation".
- UserRole has only PLATFORM_ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, ORG_MANAGER and WORKER. requireRole(...MANAGERS) grants every manager the same fields, with no permission to hide pay or document references.

Home address: confirmed minimal. Workers store postcode, lat/lng, email (set for 323 workers) and phone (set for 1). There is no street address.
impact: Pay rates are commercially sensitive, and DBS details are criminal-records data. Both are open to a competing staffing agency with no log a provider could audit. The provider cannot meet a need-to-know access policy or answer a subject-access request about who saw a worker's DBS. A data-protection officer will not sign off a data-processing agreement on these terms.
proposal:
Smallest sensible slice, in order:
1. Add a `VIEW` audit action and write an entry whenever hourlyPayRate, notes or document references are returned. Do it on GET /workers/:id (one entry per request) and on GET /workers when called by a PLATFORM_ADMIN or when the caller's org differs from the data's org (one entry for the call, with a count). The entry records actor, org, entity and fields.
2. Give each organisation's ORG_ADMIN read access to a tenant-scoped audit view (GET /organisations/:id/audit, filtered by actorOrgId or by the entity's org). This lets the provider see who looked at and who changed its workers, including operator access.
3. Stop treating PLATFORM_ADMIN as `own` in stripPrivate() and loadWorker(). By default, remove hourlyPayRate, notes and document `reference` and `notes` from the operator's responses, and show only compliance status and expiry dates. Allow full access through a time-limited, reason-required break-glass call. It writes a VIEW entry that the tenant can see, and it notifies the tenant's ORG_ADMIN.
4. Add a per-organisation field permission: two flags on users, `canViewPay` and `canViewIdentityDetails`, both set by the ORG_ADMIN. A manager without them sees compliant or not compliant and the expiry date but not the pay rate or the reference number.
5. Document in ARCHITECTURE.md that the PLATFORM_ADMIN role is separate from the agency's supplier users.
decisionNeeded: Should the operator (the agency that runs Merge, which is also a supplier on the network) be able to see tenants' worker pay rates, notes and ID or DBS references at all? If yes, on what lawful basis and DPA terms, and is it acting as processor or controller (this links to the SEC-01 question)? Does the tenant, rather than the operator, own and hold the audit trail of access to its data? And should the agency's commercial arm be run from a separate organisation or login from the platform-operator role?

title: No Microsoft sign-in, no two-factor, no lockout, weak passwords allowed, passwords that can never be changed, and leavers can still log in
persona: IT and data-protection lead evaluating Merge for a provider group
evidence:
Checked live against http://localhost:4055/api/v1 and in the code.

SSO and MFA:
- GET /auth/sso, /auth/oauth/microsoft, /auth/saml/metadata and /auth/oidc/callback all return 404.
- POST /auth/mfa/enroll and /auth/2fa/setup return 404.
- PATCH /organisations/org_1a4shuzibdsu6f4n with {requireMfa:true, ssoProvider:"microsoft", allowedEmailDomain:"northern-care-group.example"} returned 200 and the org object came back without those fields. The zod schema (zOrganisation.partial()) strips them, so there is no error and no effect.
- docs/FEATURE-ROADMAP.md:64 lists "MFA for admins, SSO (Microsoft Entra / Google)" under future work.

Lockout and audit:
- 30 wrong passwords against admin@meadow-view.example gave 30 x 401 with no throttling, and the correct password then returned 200.
- The 401 response carries no Retry-After header.
- There is no rate limiting anywhere: grep for rateLimit, throttle and helmet in apps/api/src found nothing. app.ts has only express.json({limit:'1mb'}).
- apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts only calls audit() with action LOGIN after a successful login, so failed attempts are never recorded.

Password rules:
- The only rule is z.string().min(8).max(200) in auth.ts:31, workers.ts:151 and organisations.ts:231.
- POST /auth/register returned 201 for an org admin with password "password".
- There is no breach-list or complexity check.

Passwords cannot be changed:
- POST /auth/change-password, /auth/password, /auth/logout, /auth/forgot-password and /auth/reset-password return 404.
- PATCH /auth/me and GET /auth/sessions return 404.
- PATCH /organisations/:id/users/:userId (organisations.ts ~L275) accepts only role, status, firstName and lastName. Sending {password:"NewPassw0rd!x"} alone returned 500. The old password Temp-Pass-1234 still logged in (200) and the new one returned 401. So an admin has no way to reset a password and nobody can change their own.

Tokens:
- jwtExpiresIn is '12h' (apps/api/src/config.ts:17). The JWT payload is {sub, orgId, role, iat, exp}.
- There is no refresh token, no token version and no revocation list.
- requireAuth (lib/auth.ts) re-reads the user and rejects status != ACTIVE on every request, so setting the user to DISABLED does kill existing tokens at once. That part works.
- apps/web/src/api/client.ts:31-40 stores the token in localStorage.
- Layout.tsx "Sign out" calls logout() in AuthContext, which only removes the token from the browser.

Leavers:
- PATCH /workers/:id {status:"INACTIVE"} (workers.ts ~L99) updates only the workers row. It never touches users.status.
- I deactivated worker wrk_4abe3q2bioadkkua (Finn Smith). Login as finn.smith.199@northern-care-group.example / Temp-Pass-1234 still returned 200. GET /auth/me returned 200 with worker.status INACTIVE and hourlyPayRate 12.3. GET /workers/wrk_4abe3q2bioadkkua as the worker returned 200 with documents including DBS-363353. GET /shifts returned 200. Listing other workers returned 403, so the leaver's exposure is their own record only.
- The only route to disable a login is PATCH /organisations/:id/users/:userId {status:"DISABLED"}, a separate step on the users list.
- loadWorker() in workers.ts allows the `self` path whenever user.workerId matches, with no check on worker status.

Test data left behind: I reverted Finn Smith to ACTIVE. My weak-password registration created "Weak Pw Test Ltd" (org_ndofe1paawdtd3wo, admin weak.test@example.org). I then suspended that org, but it still exists.
impact: For a provider group that has to complete the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT), a cloud system holding DBS data that admins reach with a password alone (no 2FA), with no single sign-on and no brute-force protection, will not pass. Staff need yet another password, and when someone leaves the group's Microsoft account switch-off does not reach Merge. Leavers keep access unless someone remembers a second screen.
proposal:
Smallest sensible slice, in order of effort:
1. Deactivating a worker also sets the linked users.status to DISABLED, and re-activating restores it. This is a few lines in PATCH /workers/:id and could ship with WF-02.
2. Add POST /auth/change-password (current and new password) and an admin-reset endpoint on PATCH /organisations/:id/users/:userId. Fix the 500 on an empty update body. Add users.tokenVersion and put it in the JWT so password changes and "sign out all sessions" invalidate existing tokens. Add POST /auth/logout that bumps the version.
3. Password policy: minimum 12 characters, a breach-list or common-password check, and a shared zPassword validator used in register, worker login, org user create and change-password.
4. Login throttling: per-email and per-IP attempt counter, a temporary lockout with a Retry-After header, and a LOGIN_FAILED audit event.
5. Organisation setting requireMfa, with TOTP enrolment and challenge at login, enforced for ORG_ADMIN, ORG_MANAGER and PLATFORM_ADMIN.
6. OIDC sign-in with Microsoft Entra per organisation, tied to allowedEmailDomain, with an optional "SSO only" switch that disables password login for that org.
Items 1 to 4 are small and local. 5 and 6 are the larger pieces and need the decision below.
decisionNeeded: Should 2FA be compulsory for every admin and manager on the platform, or an option each organisation turns on? Which identity providers are needed at launch (Microsoft Entra only, or Google too)? Should SSO-enforced organisations lose password login entirely? What lockout policy should apply, for example attempts, window and unlock method, given that password reset by email does not exist yet (ONB-04)?

title: Any worker login can read a colleague's pay, DBS number and postcode, and add or remove that colleague's unavailability
persona: IT and data-protection lead evaluating Merge for a provider group
evidence: Reproduced live as harry.mensah.730@riverside-living.example (role WORKER, Riverside) at http://localhost:4055. (1) GET /workers returns 403, so the list is blocked as intended. (2) GET /workers/wrk_yrjuztt1jbaezsfy, /workers/wrk_dx23oyn6r8joyz9f and /workers/wrk_5c0gaqhegbi549dq each return 200. They carry hourlyPayRate 13.5, 13.5 and 12.3, postcodes M41 6JL, M41 6TW and M41 8QR, and a documents[] array with DBS references DBS-336915, DBS-332852 and DBS-666688. The response also includes unavailability, upcoming shifts, averageRating, login and notes. These values match the finding and the manager's own list view. (3) POST /workers/wrk_yrjuztt1jbaezsfy/unavailability returned 201, and the Riverside admin then saw the entry on that worker. DELETE returned 204. I removed my test entry afterwards. (4) The POST and DELETE handlers (workers.ts around lines 222-262) contain no auditFromReq call. Every other mutating worker route does call it. DELETE has no self or own check beyond loadWorker, so the same bug applies to it. (5) The boundary holds elsewhere: a worker gets 403 for an Oakwood worker (GET and POST unavailability), and 403 for PATCH /workers/:id and POST /workers/:id/documents on a colleague, because those use requireRole(MANAGERS). The hole is limited to GET /:id, POST unavailability and DELETE unavailability. (6) Notes leak: GET /auth/me (auth.ts lines 92-100) returns the full unstripped workers row to the worker, including notes. GET /workers/:self also returns notes because own is true. I did not seed a note to prove it live, but the code path is unconditional, so the persona's leaver observation is consistent. (7) No test covers this: apps/api/test/api.test.ts line 339 only checks cross-organisation 403, and lines 317 and 388 cover a worker's own shifts, timesheets and assignments, not GET /workers/:id.
impact: This is broken access control that a penetration test would flag straight away. Colleagues' pay and criminal-records references can leak between staff. A worker can quietly block a colleague from shifts by adding unavailability, and nothing records who did it.
proposal: Smallest fix, all in apps/api/src/routes/workers.ts plus one line in auth.ts. (a) In loadWorker, set own = isPlatformAdmin(req) || (MANAGERS.includes(user.role) && w.orgId === user.orgId). Keep self as is, and throw forbidden when neither applies. (b) For a self-only caller, GET /:id returns a self view: strip notes (and decide on hourlyPayRate), and do not return other workers' data. Apply the same strip to the worker object returned by /auth/me. (c) Allow unavailability POST and DELETE only for managers of the employer or the worker themselves (self), with a worker-ownership check on DELETE. (d) Add auditFromReq on unavailability create and delete, recording the actor. (e) Add tests: a worker gets 403 on a colleague's GET, POST unavailability and DELETE unavailability; a worker's own GET and /auth/me contain no employer notes; unavailability changes write audit rows. Update docs/API.md if the self view differs.
decisionNeeded: Should a worker see their own hourlyPayRate? Should they see the employer's private notes about them? Showing notes is a UK GDPR subject-access question and may need HR review before the field is exposed, so the safe default is to strip notes from the worker's own view and handle access to them through the data-subject work in SEC-01.

title: The audit log cannot show what one user did last month
persona: IT and data-protection lead evaluating Merge for a provider group
evidence:
Checked live (clock 2027-05-03T08:00Z) and against code and a read-only copy of apps/api/data/sim.db.

Tenant access (Northern Care Group org admin, admin@northern-care-group.example):
- GET /admin/audit returns 403.
- GET /audit, /organisations/:id/audit, /organisations/:id/activity, /organisations/:id/users/:uid/activity, /me/activity, /activity, /audit-log and /organisations/:id/audit-log all return 404.
- The web app has no tenant audit screen. The only audit UI is AuditTable in apps/web/src/pages/AdminPage.tsx, reached through the platform-only /admin route (apps/web/src/App.tsx line 59: RequireAuth platform).

Platform admin (owner@merge-staffing.example):
- GET /admin/audit?limit=500 returns 200 with 500 rows from 24 distinct actors.
- Adding actorUserId=usr_8hfiii9vrb03c569&from=2027-04-01&to=2027-04-30 returns the same 500 rows from the same 24 actors. The extra parameters are ignored.
- limit=1000 returns 400. offset=100 is ignored. entityType=user&entityId=usr_8hfiii9vrb03c569 returns 14 rows, which are actions on that user (LOGINs plus one CREATE), not actions by that user.
- The newest 500 rows all carry the 08:00:00 instant on 3 May. The simulation clock is frozen, so my own and other verifiers' logins fill the window, and rows older than a day or two are unreachable. sim.db holds 32,152 rows now (the finding said 31,929; the difference is logins made during verification) and 730 of them fall on 3 May alone.

Ground truth in sim.db for rota@northern-care-group.example (usr_8hfiii9vrb03c569), 1 to 30 April 2027: 351 rows. They are 69 shift CREATE, 69 shift PUBLISH, 62 timesheet APPROVE, 58 shift_assignment CONFIRM, 50 shift_assignment REQUEST, 24 timesheet UPDATE, 9 capacity_flag CREATE, 4 timesheet DISPUTE, 3 DECLINE and 3 shift_assignment UPDATE. None can be retrieved through the API.

Indexes: audit_log has only (entity_type, entity_id) and (created_at) indexes (apps/api/src/db/schema.ts lines 392-405). There is no actor index, so adding an actor filter also needs a new index.

Not logged at all:
- Failed logins: /auth/login throws unauthorized before the audit() call (apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts lines 74-86).
- Reads of worker records.
- Worker unavailability add and delete: workers.ts lines 221-238 have no auditFromReq call.

Web display: AuditTable filters by entity type only, limits to 200 rows, shows the actor as a raw user ID (a.actorUserId), and has no export.
impact: After a safeguarding incident, a disciplinary case or a suspected breach, a provider cannot produce what a named manager did. Only the agency can try, and even the agency can see only the last day or two. The provider cannot meet its accountability duty under UK GDPR or answer the regulator.
proposal:
Smallest useful slice, in three parts.

1. API.
- Add GET /organisations/:id/audit, org admin only, scoped to audit_log.actor_org_id = :id.
- Filters: actorUserId, from, to, entityType, action.
- Cursor pagination: limit up to 500 plus a before/cursor on (createdAt, id).
- Join users so each row returns actor name and email.
- Add a ?format=csv option.
- Add an index on audit_log (actor_user_id, created_at) and one on (actor_org_id, created_at).
- Give /admin/audit the same filters and cursor, which is a few lines in admin.ts.

2. Web.
- Add an Activity tab, or an Audit log card, under Settings > Users, with a user filter, a date range and CSV download. Resolve actor names instead of showing IDs.

3. New events.
- Add LOGIN_FAILED (and optionally LOGOUT) to the AuditAction enum and write it in /auth/login.
- Audit unavailability create and delete.
- Audit reads of worker records, but see the decision below before building this, because it adds volume.

Keep the first release to parts 1 and 2 plus failed logins. Sensitive-read logging can follow once the volume and retention decision is made.
decisionNeeded: 1) Should tenants see only actions taken by their own users, or also actions agency staff took on their data (for example the agency verifying a document for them)? 2) How long should audit rows be kept, and does logging reads of worker records (high volume, special-category data) justify its storage cost? This ties to the controller-versus-processor and retention question already open under SEC-01. 3) Should org managers have access, or org admins only?

title: No safe way to connect the group's rota system: no API keys, service accounts, webhooks or rate limits
persona: IT and data-protection lead evaluating Merge for a provider group
evidence:
VERIFIED, by calling the API as admin@northern-care-group.example and rota@northern-care-group.example.
- Missing endpoints: GET and POST on /api/v1/api-keys, /organisations/:id/api-keys, /organisations/:id/webhooks, /webhooks, /integrations, /auth/token, /auth/refresh and /auth/change-password all return 404. /openapi.json, /api/openapi.json and /api/v1/openapi.json return 404. The only reference is prose in docs/API.md.
- No integration role: POST /organisations/:id/users with role INTEGRATION returns 400 ("Expected 'ORG_ADMIN' | 'ORG_MANAGER' | 'WORKER' | 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'"). The enum is in apps/api/src/routes/organisations.ts around line 232.
- Token lifetime: the JWT for rota@northern-care-group.example decodes to exp - iat = 12.0 h. Config default is jwtExpiresIn '12h' (apps/api/src/config.ts), there is no refresh endpoint, and tokens are stateless so there is no revocation list. An integration must log in again with the stored password every 12 h.
- No password rotation: PATCH /organisations/:id/users/:userId with {"password":"..."} returns 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}. The zod schema (organisations.ts around line 259) has no password field, so the unknown key is stripped and db.update(users).set({}) throws. No other route changes a password; grep shows only hashPassword at create and verifyPassword at login. So a shared integration password can never be rotated, and neither can anyone's own password.
- Over-broad rights: the manager role (rota@) gets full write rights, because assignments.ts routes use requireRole(...MANAGERS) for confirm, decline and cancel (lines 82, 144, 161, 177). GET /workers returns 415 workers including hourlyPayRate (e.g. 12.5). GET /workers/:id returns documents including DBS type, reference and expiry. There are no scopes and no read-only role.
- Audit gap: audit entries record actorUserId, so the integration appears as an ordinary user. The audit log endpoint GET /admin/audit sits behind requireRole(PLATFORM_ADMIN) in apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts line 13. Both the Northern Care org admin and the rota manager get 403, so the group's own IT lead cannot review what the integration did. Only Merge's platform admin can.
- No polling support: GET /assignments accepts only scope and status (assignments.ts line 41). I passed updatedSince and from, and the result stayed at 918 rows, so unknown params are silently ignored. GET /shifts does have from, to, status and jobRole filters (shifts.ts lines 64-75), so the finding should say "assignments has no date or updatedSince filter", not the whole API. No endpoint offers updatedSince, and there is no push of any kind: grep finds no webhook code. The only mention is a comment in lib/notify.ts line 16 listing webhook as a possible future channel.
- No rate limiting: 60 sequential authenticated GET /assignments?status=CONFIRMED calls all returned 200 in 0.56 s. The response headers carry no X-RateLimit-* or Retry-After. app.ts has no limiter middleware (only cors and express.json limit 1mb).
- NEW angle, no login throttling: 30 wrong-password POSTs to /auth/login for a real manager account all returned 401 with no 429 and no lockout, and the correct password still worked afterwards. Nothing in apps/api/src matches lockout, throttle or attempt. This matters more because the integration's identity is a password.
impact: Rotas are typed in twice and drift apart, or IT has to keep a shared manager password in an integration server with more access than it needs and no way to rotate or scope it. With no rate limits, one buggy integration can overload the service for everyone.
proposal:
Smallest sensible phase one, in priority order.
1. Per-organisation API clients, created by an ORG_ADMIN. Each has a name and a long random secret shown once, stored hashed. It carries a fixed read-only scope such as read:shifts and read:assignments, can be revoked or rotated, and is bound to its own org. Add a new principal type or role (INTEGRATION) that the auth middleware accepts via Authorization: Bearer or X-Api-Key and that never has write access in phase one. Record the client id as the audit actor.
2. Let org admins read their own organisation's audit entries, filtered to the integration client and to their own users. Today GET /admin/audit is platform-admin only.
3. Add updatedAt and an updatedSince query filter, plus from and to, to GET /assignments and GET /shifts. Add a stable id and updatedAt on every row so a poller can sync incrementally.
4. Add a basic limiter (for example 120 requests per minute per credential and per IP) that returns 429, Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers. Include throttling or lockout on /auth/login.
5. Add POST /auth/change-password. Make admin PATCH ignore or reject unknown keys with a 400 instead of a 500 (use strict zod) and support an admin-initiated password reset.
6. Publish an OpenAPI document generated from the zod schemas, served at /api/v1/openapi.json.
Phase two: HMAC-signed webhooks (assignment.confirmed, assignment.cancelled, shift.updated, timesheet.approved) with retries, delivered through the existing Notifier channel interface in lib/notify.ts, then scoped write rights (for example write:unavailability).
decisionNeeded: Which rota systems must be supported first (RotaCloud, Access, PCS, CarePlanner are named on the roadmap), and is a read-only feed of confirmed bookings enough for phase one, or must the rota system also write back (import gaps as draft shifts, push unavailability)? Also, should org admins be allowed to see their own organisation's audit trail, which is currently platform-admin only?
